guides.title: Best Time to Visit Thailand's Islands: Month by Month
guides.summary: Compare Koh Samui and Phuket weather month by month. Choose the Gulf or Andaman islands using TMD climate normals, with advice for ferries and rough seas.
guides.html:
Choose the coast before the month

For Koh Samui, Koh Phangan and Koh Tao, start by comparing the southern Gulf with the Andaman coast. Their rain calendars differ. Our editorial starting point is February for a trip combining both coasts, the Samui archipelago for June to September, and the Andaman islands for December and January. None of these choices guarantees a dry week or a calm crossing.

On the Andaman side, compare Phuket, Koh Phi Phi, Koh Lanta and Koh Lipe, or the mainland gateway of Krabi. Use our island comparison to choose a base before adding transfers.

The station data, and its limits

The table uses Thai Meteorological Department climate normals for 1991 to 2020: Ko Samui station 48550 and Phuket station 48564. Phuket here means the station named Phuket, not Phuket Airport. High means the monthly mean daily maximum air temperature in degrees Celsius; rain means the monthly mean rainfall total in millimetres. These are climate averages, not a forecast.

Ko Samui is a reference for the archipelago, not a separate measurement for Phangan or Tao. Phuket is a reference for the Andaman comparison, not a measurement for every western island. Neither station measures the conditions on your particular beach or ferry route. The last column is our editorial recommendation based on these rainfall comparisons, with extra caution in October.

How to use the monthly choices

Read across your travel month rather than treating Thailand as one beach season. At Ko Samui station, October to December have the three highest monthly rainfall totals; at Phuket station, May to October are the six wettest months. These station patterns inform our coast comparison, without measuring each island separately. February is the driest month at both named stations, making it our simplest starting point for a trip combining the Gulf and Andaman.

If your dates are fixed, choose the recommended coast first and compare islands within it. If the island is fixed, use its station column to decide how much flexibility to leave. For an island-focused trip, compare Samui, Phangan and Tao; for a choice between coasts, read Samui versus Phuket.

Sea conditions and ferry disruption

Rainfall totals are not wave forecasts. A bright morning is not a reason to disregard a marine warning. The Thai government's monsoon explainer, credited to TMD, places the southwest monsoon roughly from mid-May to mid-October and the northeast monsoon from mid-October to mid-February. Strong monsoon episodes can bring rough seas: TMD has issued upper-Andaman wave warnings in May and Gulf wave warnings in December.

For planning, treat May to October on the Andaman coast and October to December around Samui, Phangan and Tao as periods to leave extra room for weather-related disruption. This is a precaution based on the monsoon cycle and rain pattern, not a measured ranking of ferry cancellations. Keep checking Gulf marine forecasts in January and February too, while the northeast monsoon can still be active.

Lomprayah's published terms allow weather-related timetable and route changes without notice. Check the operating company's own updates before each crossing, alongside TMD's marine forecast. Do not infer that all boats stop for an entire rainy season, or that a booking guarantees a sailing.

  • Our recommendation is to avoid a last possible ferry connection before an important flight.
  • Leave a spare night before an international departure when the itinerary depends on a boat.
  • Keep a land-based alternative for a planned Ang Thong day trip or snorkelling excursion.
  • Use the Samui, Phangan and Tao ferry guide when building the route, then recheck the operator for your actual date.

Swimming, snorkelling and diving

Choose a swim or boat excursion using the day's conditions and local instructions, not the monthly coast recommendation alone. For diving, discuss the day's sites and conditions with the dive team before committing. This guide does not promise visibility, animal sightings or calm water in a particular month. The air temperatures above are not sea temperatures.

Keep beach days flexible within a Samui itinerary or Tao itinerary. Put your most important boat activity early enough in the stay to allow another attempt, subject to availability and conditions.

Koh Chang needs its own check

Do not extend the Ko Samui station figures to every island labelled Gulf of Thailand. For Koh Chang, use a local forecast and the destination overview before choosing dates. The two-station table is a southern Gulf versus Andaman comparison, not a climate table for the Eastern Gulf.

Prices and trip length

Compare rooms and transport for your exact dates. We do not label an entire month cheapest or quietest without comparable booking data. If weather flexibility matters more than seeing several islands, our suggestion is to spend seven to fourteen days on one coast with fewer transfers. Treat that as an itinerary choice rather than a required trip length.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the best month for a first Thai islands trip?

Our recommendation is February if you want the option of either coast. Compare your preferred islands and the daily forecast before making the final choice.

Which coast should I choose in July or August?

Our starting choice is the Samui archipelago. Use the monthly comparison above, then allow for changing conditions rather than expecting rain-free days.

Should I choose Phuket or Samui for December?

Our weather-led choice is Phuket and the Andaman coast. That is a relative preference, not a promise that December will be dry.

Can ferries be disrupted outside the rainy months?

Do not treat any month as disruption-proof. Check the operator's notices and marine forecast for the crossing itself, and protect important onward connections with spare time.

Does rainy season mean it rains all day?

A monthly rainfall total does not tell you when rain will fall during your stay. Use the climate table to choose dates and the short-range forecast to organise individual days.

guides.title: Full Moon Party Guide and Dates: Koh Phangan
guides.summary: The Full Moon Party takes place at Haad Rin on Koh Phangan. Check the party date before booking, choose accommodation and arrange the journey home together.
guides.html:
Start with the island and the party date

The Full Moon Party is on Koh Phangan, at Haad Rin's Sunrise Beach, Haad Rin Nok. It is not on Koh Samui. If your bed is on Koh Samui, include a sea crossing in both directions when planning the night.

The schedule publisher warns that dates can change following local or government announcements. The schedule below is published by Official Full Moon Party at fullmoonpartythailand.com, which says its dates are issued by the Haad Rin Business Association and its page is maintained by local business members. Treat the dates as announced, then recheck with your accommodation and transport operator before paying for non-refundable travel. This guide was checked on 16 November 2026.

Announced dates for the coming months

As of November 2026, the publisher lists these dates. Each row names the schedule used; these are party dates, not an astronomical full-moon calendar.

Announced dateSchedule publisher
24 November 2026Official Full Moon Party, Haad Rin community schedule
24 December 2026Official Full Moon Party, Haad Rin community schedule
22 January 2027Official Full Moon Party, Haad Rin community schedule
22 February 2027Official Full Moon Party, Haad Rin community schedule
22 March 2027Official Full Moon Party, Haad Rin community schedule

Recheck the announced date shortly before departure. Do not calculate your trip from a moon-phase app or assume a party will fall on the same date in another year.

Why Buddhist holidays can move the party

The community schedule reports a March 2026 decision to move parties that coincide with a major Buddhist holy day to the following day. Its February 2027 listing places the party after Makha Bucha. Use the announced event date rather than trying to apply that rule yourself to a future calendar.

Alcohol restrictions also need a current check. As of November 2026, Thailand's government information portal says sales remain restricted on five major Buddhist holidays, with exemptions for specified establishments, including qualifying hotels and licensed entertainment venues. That does not establish that every beach seller or party venue is exempt. Ask the venue about the rules for your date and follow local announcements. See our Thailand public holidays guide for broader planning.

Entry fee and what to budget separately

As of November 2026, the Haad Rin community's Official Full Moon Party page lists entry at THB 200, with tickets available only at the entry gate. Budget separately for your room, transport, food and drinks. Before buying any transfer package, ask whether beach admission is included and how the return journey works.

Getting to Haad Rin from Koh Samui

As of November 2026, a published scheduled-ferry option is Seatran Discovery from Bangrak Pier on Koh Samui to Thong Sala Pier on Koh Phangan. The operator describes onward shared taxis, called songthaews, and private transfers to Haad Rin. A ticket to Thong Sala gets you to the port, so arrange the road journey to the party as well. Check the operator's current booking page for the actual departure pier, sailing and fare on your date.

Seatran Discovery recommends advance booking around Full Moon Party periods. For this guide, the practical recommendation is to cross before the party, leave time to reach your accommodation and arrange your return before going out. Do not assume your daytime ferry ticket includes a late-night sailing back. Compare an overnight stay on Koh Phangan with any return boat offer, including its boarding point and cancellation arrangements. Our ferry guide covers the wider island route.

Getting there from elsewhere on Koh Phangan

From Thong Sala and Baan Tai, arrange a songthaew or private transfer to Haad Rin. Agree the total price, whether it is per person or per vehicle, the drop-off point and the return meeting place before leaving. Ask your accommodation to arrange a pickup if you are staying around Srithanu and the west coast or Thong Nai Pan; confirm the route and availability for that evening.

Save your accommodation address offline and keep enough money aside for the journey home. The planning recommendation here is to use a prearranged driver rather than make a scooter your party-night transport.

Where to stay and when to book

Start your room search in Haad Rin if your priority is staying near the event. Confirm the actual walking route from the room to the beach and ask about party-night noise. For a stay based elsewhere, compare Baan Tai or Thong Sala and price the return transfer before deciding. Use our Koh Phangan accommodation guide to compare areas.

The Full Moon Haad Rin community website recommends booking accommodation early. Make a shortlist once you have chosen an announced date, check cancellation terms and ask each property about any minimum stay. There is no universal booking deadline or minimum-night rule quoted here. A flexible room reservation is a useful precaution while you reconfirm the party and ferry dates.

Safety and law: advice to read before the night

Government travel advice checked as of November 2026 should guide your decisions:

  • Drinks and company: Australian Smartraveller advises keeping drinks attended and staying with trusted people at parties and in taxis. Agree a meeting place with your companions.
  • Boats and swimming: Smartraveller advises avoiding boat travel after dark, wearing a lifejacket and refusing overcrowded boats. After drinking, avoid swimming or boarding a boat. Plan an overnight stay accordingly and accept weather cancellations.
  • Drugs: UK FCDO advice warns of severe penalties for illegal drug possession. It says cannabis is restricted to medical use with a Thai-issued prescription; do not treat shop availability as permission.
  • Vapes: FCDO says possessing or using vapes, e-cigarettes, pods, e-liquids or heat-not-burn devices is illegal in Thailand.
  • Scooters: FCDO says motorcycle helmets are compulsory. For UK licence holders it specifies a UK driving licence plus a 1968 International Driving Permit. Check the correct vehicle entitlement and insurance terms; driving without a valid licence can invalidate cover.

Recheck government travel advice before travelling. Keep our emergency contacts page saved for help during the trip.

Half Moon and other parties

Half Moon Festival is a separate event in Baan Tai on Koh Phangan, with its own organiser, tickets and dates. Its organiser advertises a venue change specifically for 17 November 2026, so verify the venue as well as the date for the edition you plan to attend. For any other party, check the organiser's current announcement and entry arrangements separately. A Full Moon Party beach ticket should not be assumed to cover another event.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the Full Moon Party on Koh Samui?

No. It is at Haad Rin on Koh Phangan. From Koh Samui, arrange a sea crossing and the onward journey to the beach.

Can I rely on a full-moon calendar?

Use the published party schedule and reconfirm it before travel. Buddhist observances can shift the party away from the astronomical full moon.

Should I book a room before my ferry?

Check both together. Choose an announced party date, find a suitable room with cancellation terms you understand, then confirm the crossings and road transfers that make the stay work.

guides.title: How to Get to Koh Samui: Flights, Trains and Ferries
guides.summary: Choose an arrival route to Koh Samui and understand the difference between Nathon, Lipa Noi, Bangrak and Maenam before booking your onward island transfer.
guides.html:
To reach Koh Samui (also written Ko Samui), compare a flight to Samui Airport (USM) with a mainland journey followed by a ferry. Bangkok Airways publishes direct routes from Bangkok and Phuket. For travel from Krabi, compare the road and ferry options below and ask the airline about flights for your date. Mainland alternatives include Surat Thani Airport, Chumphon Airport, a train to Surat Thani and combined coach and ferry journeys.

Checked as of November 2026: this is a route-planning guide, not a live departure board. Lomprayah currently warns of temporary schedule and pier changes from 5 November to 5 December 2026. Confirm the terminal for your particular sailing before arranging a collection. We give no fixed fares or departure times where the operator's current information could not be confirmed.

Choose the journey you want to make

Starting pointOptionWhat to book
BangkokDirect flight to USMBangkok Airways from Suvarnabhumi (BKK) or Don Mueang (DMK), then an island transfer
BangkokFlight to Surat Thani, then road and ferryA flight plus an airport-to-Samui connection, with the arrival pier specified
BangkokFlight to Chumphon, then road and ferryA flight plus Lomprayah's Chumphon Airport joint bus/van and catamaran ticket
BangkokOvernight train, road transfer and ferryA State Railway of Thailand train to Surat Thani, then a station-to-island connection
BangkokBus and ferryLomprayah's combined journey via Chumphon, or a road journey to the Surat Thani/Donsak gateway and a ferry
PhuketDirect flight or road and ferryBangkok Airways to USM, or a combined mainland transfer and sailing
KrabiRoad and ferryBook a combined mainland transfer and sailing; investigate flights separately rather than assuming a direct service

Compare the full cost to your accommodation: baggage, transfers to the departure point, the boat and the final island transfer. A lower air fare to a mainland airport is only one part of the price. If avoiding a ferry matters more than the ticket price, start with a flight into USM.

Bangkok to Koh Samui by direct flight

Bangkok Airways explicitly lists direct flights from both Suvarnabhumi (BKK) and Don Mueang (DMK) to Samui Airport. Check the airport code before paying, particularly when connecting from an international flight. Do not treat the two Bangkok airports as interchangeable.

For an onward flight bought separately, allow for baggage collection and check-in rather than assuming your luggage will transfer. Ask the airline about the connection before booking. Once on Samui, arrange transport to your actual accommodation in Chaweng, Lamai, Bophut or Maenam. Our Koh Samui accommodation-area guide helps you choose the destination for that transfer.

Fly to Surat Thani, then take the bus and ferry

Thai AirAsia's newsroom lists Surat Thani among its connections via Don Mueang. Check the airline for a flight on your date. Select Surat Thani Airport as the air destination, then book the road and sea connection separately unless your booking explicitly includes it. Raja Ferry's current website lists a combined Surat Thani Airport to Koh Samui journey arriving at Lipa Noi. Seatran also advertises Surat Thani airport and city coach services connecting with its ferries.

For the Donsak route, the sequence is airport, road transfer, mainland ferry terminal, then Samui. Seatran Ferry uses Nathon; Raja Ferry uses Lipa Noi. Ask which company's Donsak terminal your transfer serves. Do not book a generic transfer to Donsak and assume it delivers you to the boat on your ticket.

Lomprayah's published network also includes Surat Thani Airport and Samui connections. Choose the exact arrival terminal in its booking result, then recheck it against the temporary pier notice. Before buying the flight, ask the ferry operator which airport arrival it can accept for your date. If your flight misses the connection, plan for a mainland overnight rather than assuming another boat will be available.

Fly to Chumphon, then continue by bus and ferry

Thai AirAsia lists direct connections from Bangkok Don Mueang to Chumphon in its newsroom. Check availability for your date. Lomprayah advertises a joint bus/van and catamaran ticket from Chumphon Airport to Koh Samui. Book to Samui, rather than choosing an intermediate island simply because it appears first in the search.

Lomprayah describes its network as linking Chumphon, Koh Tao, Koh Phangan and Samui. Check the stops and any change of vessel on your specific journey. This route is worth comparing if you also want to visit the other Gulf islands; use our Samui, Phangan and Tao ferry guide for that part of the trip. Do not assume that the airport transfer and boat automatically connect with every flight.

Bangkok to Koh Samui by overnight train and ferry

Take a State Railway of Thailand overnight service from Krung Thep Aphiwat in Bangkok to Surat Thani, then continue by road and ferry. The Tourism Authority of Thailand's rail guide describes this Bangkok to Samui itinerary, with Surat Thani station and Donsak as the mainland stages. Its printed timetable is dated July 2025, so check current services and sleeper availability with the railway rather than using those old times.

Choose a sleeper berth if that is what you want, rather than assuming every overnight ticket includes a bed. Book the station-to-Samui connection explicitly. Raja's booking menu includes Surat Thani railway station and Lipa Noi, while Lomprayah's timetable includes station connections. Leave room for a late train when selecting the boat.

A Chumphon rail connection is another route to investigate with Lomprayah, whose website lists Chumphon train connections into its island network. Confirm a through journey to Samui before reserving the train. We could not confirm a current overnight train and ferry combination via Chumphon with matched departure times, so do not build a tight connection from this guide.

Bangkok to Koh Samui by bus and ferry

Lomprayah states that its Bangkok connection uses an air-conditioned bus from Chumphon. Its website lists Bangkok departures under both Khaosan and Pinklao, so use the address on your booking rather than turning up at a bus terminal from memory. Compare an overnight combined journey with the train option if you want to travel through the night.

The other approach is to travel by road towards Surat Thani or Donsak and take Seatran Ferry to Nathon or Raja Ferry to Lipa Noi. Raja's booking menu also includes Bangkok departure points. Verify the company operating each leg and whether the fare includes the ferry before paying. A combined ticket does not by itself tell you whether you stay on the same vehicle, change buses or carry your luggage between them.

Phuket to Koh Samui

By air: Bangkok Airways confirms direct flights from Phuket Airport (HKT) to USM. Compare this with a road and sea journey when you have limited time. Include the transfer from your Phuket accommodation to HKT in that comparison.

By road and ferry: Lomprayah's timetable includes Phuket to Samui combinations, and Raja's booking menu includes Phuket Bus Terminal 2. Confirm the pickup point and Samui arrival pier for your date. You can also arrange a road transfer to the appropriate Donsak terminal and book Seatran Ferry or Raja Ferry separately. This is a road-and-sea journey, so do not read a Phuket to Samui ferry listing as a promise of a boat running all the way from Phuket.

Krabi to Koh Samui

Investigating flights: ask Bangkok Airways about travel from Krabi Airport (KBV) to USM for your date. The airline publishes a direct Samui-to-Krabi route, but that does not establish a service in the opposite direction. Its Krabi-to-Samui page returned a page-not-found message during this check. We therefore do not confirm a direct flight from Krabi to Samui.

By road and ferry: Lomprayah's timetable lists Krabi combinations arriving at Samui's Nathon Pier. Raja's booking menu includes Krabi Bus Terminal and Ao Nang departure points. Confirm the actual meeting point, especially if you are staying outside Krabi town, and ask whether hotel collection is included. A separately arranged road transfer to Donsak plus Seatran Ferry or Raja Ferry is another way to assemble the journey. See the Krabi overview when planning where to start.

Which Samui pier does each operator use?

These names reflect the operators' published information read as of November 2026. They describe different arrival points, not interchangeable names for a single Samui ferry terminal.

Samui pierOperator informationBooking implication
NathonSeatran Ferry identifies its Samui terminal as Nathon. Lomprayah also lists Nathon, including Krabi connections.Specify the operator as well as Nathon when arranging collection.
Lipa NoiRaja Ferry lists Donsak to Koh Samui (Lipa Noi pier), and its airport connection also arrives here.Give your driver Lipa Noi, not simply Samui ferry pier.
BangrakSeatran Discovery explicitly names its Bangrak terminal. Lomprayah also advertises catamaran services from Bangrak.Seatran Discovery and Seatran Ferry are different service names with different Samui terminals. Use the exact operator and map pin on your ticket.
Maenam, Pralarn PierLomprayah's timetable uses Pralarn. Its contact page lists Pralan Pier at an address in Maenam.Reconfirm the sailing's terminal: Lomprayah currently has temporary pier changes.

Temporary Lomprayah changes: the homepage notice covers 5 November to 5 December 2026 and asks passengers to check in 60 minutes before departure. The detailed notice did not load in readable form during our check, so we cannot identify every affected sailing here. Ask Lomprayah to confirm your boarding or arrival pier in writing. Do not assume the general timetable overrides the notice, or that every service changes pier.

Songserm's own website confirms services linking Samui, Phangan and Tao, but we could not confirm a named Samui pier from the operator material we read. We therefore do not assign Songserm to a terminal in this table.

Before you pay

  • Check the airport code, road pickup address and exact Samui arrival pier.
  • Ask which transfers are included and where you must handle your own luggage.
  • Compare the total journey to your accommodation, not just the first ticket.
  • Recheck operator notices before departure and keep flexibility before a separately booked flight home.

For the next stage, our five-day Koh Samui itinerary starts your island planning, while the ten-day Gulf island itinerary joins Samui with Phangan and Tao.

guides.title: Koh Samui, Koh Phangan and Koh Tao Ferry Guide
guides.summary: Plan ferries between Koh Samui, Koh Phangan and Koh Tao: compare piers and boat types, check luggage rules and prepare for monsoon disruption before booking.
guides.html:
Travelling between Koh Samui, Koh Phangan and Koh Tao means choosing a boat and a specific pier, not simply an island name. Lomprayah advertises high-speed catamarans linking the three islands. Seatran Discovery publishes passenger routes from Bangrak on Koh Samui to Thong Sala on Koh Phangan and Mae Haad on Koh Tao. Songserm also advertises connections between these islands.

Travel notice, November 2026: Lomprayah has announced temporary schedule and pier changes from 5 November to 5 December 2026. Reconfirm the exact pier and sailing before arranging a transfer.

Information below was read on operator pages on 16 November 2026. Published crossing durations are planning estimates, not guaranteed arrival times. Select your travel date on the operator's booking site before arranging a transfer. We have not reproduced clock-time departures or route fares where the current offer could not be confirmed.

Which operator should you check?

Lomprayah is a starting point for a passenger journey across all three islands. Its route overview lists Koh Samui to Koh Phangan and Koh Phangan to Koh Tao. Its Koh Samui contact page lists Pralan Pier in Maenam and Nathon Pier, and a current announcement also advertises catamarans from Bangrak. Read the departure pier in your actual booking: do not assume that every Lomprayah sailing leaves from Maenam.

Seatran Discovery publishes Bangrak to Thong Sala and Bangrak to Mae Haad routes. Its Koh Tao article says the journey often stops at Koh Phangan. If booking for Koh Tao, ask whether you remain aboard or change boats on your chosen departure.

Songserm describes connections between Koh Samui, Koh Phangan and Koh Tao and offers online reservations. Check its date-specific booking results for the pier, vessel and baggage conditions. We could not confirm a current route-by-route timetable or luggage weight allowance from the page read.

Raja Ferry is relevant when investigating travel with a vehicle. Its booking form includes vehicle categories. As of November 2026, its sailing-information page describes Lipa Noi on Koh Samui to Thong Sala on Koh Phangan as approximately 1 hour 30 minutes, but this is a route description rather than confirmation of an available departure. However, its FAQ lists Donsak to Samui and Donsak to Phangan, while the vehicle-booking form read did not clearly offer a direct Samui to Phangan selection. Ask Raja to confirm that the direct crossing is operating and accepts your vehicle on your date before relying on it.

Piers on each island

IslandPiers to recogniseBooking check
Koh SamuiPralan Pier in Maenam, Nathon, Bangrak and Lipa NoiLomprayah lists Pralan and Nathon and advertises Bangrak services. Seatran Discovery's routes here specify Bangrak. Raja uses Lipa Noi.
Koh PhanganThong SalaSeatran Discovery names Thong Sala; Raja's sailing page names it too. Check the operator's exact check-in point.
Koh TaoMae HaadSeatran Discovery explicitly names Mae Haad as its Koh Tao arrival and check-in pier. Confirm the pier on any other operator's ticket.

For accommodation planning, read about Maenam on Koh Samui, Thong Sala on Koh Phangan and Sairee and Mae Haad on Koh Tao. Put the operator's pier pin into your transfer booking. If staying in Haad Rin, check the arrival pier rather than treating the beach name as a ferry destination.

Published crossing durations

As of November 2026, the operators' pages give the following durations. These describe particular services, not every boat between the same islands.

JourneyOperatorPublished duration
Koh Samui to Koh PhanganLomprayah30 minutes in its route overview; confirm the pier and selected sailing.
Koh Phangan to Koh TaoLomprayah1 hour in its route overview.
Bangrak, Koh Samui, to Thong Sala, Koh PhanganSeatran DiscoveryAround 30 to 45 minutes.
Bangrak, Koh Samui, to Mae Haad, Koh TaoSeatran DiscoveryApproximately 2 to 2.5 hours, often with a Koh Phangan stop.

Do not add two published segment durations and assume that they form a bookable connection. Check the complete journey, including any wait or boat change. For a trip with nights on each island, use our Samui, Phangan and Tao itinerary as a planning framework and buy transport around the sailings actually offered.

Vehicle ferries versus catamarans

Lomprayah calls its service a high-speed catamaran. Raja's booking form distinguishes foot passengers from vehicles, including motorcycles and cars. A passenger booking is not confirmation of a vehicle space: if taking a car or scooter, obtain a booking that explicitly identifies the vehicle, route and departure.

For Samui to Phangan, resolve the discrepancy between Raja's sailing-information page and booking choices before making plans. We could not confirm a vehicle-ferry service to Koh Tao from the operator pages read. Plan that leg as a foot passenger unless an operating company confirms otherwise. For a hired vehicle, ask the rental company in writing whether the proposed ferry journey is permitted and what its cover includes.

How to buy tickets

  1. Search the operating company's website. Lomprayah, Seatran Discovery and Songserm have online booking options. Raja lists website and app bookings as well as sales at its Donsak, Lipa Noi and Thong Sala piers.
  2. Select the date and exact route. Check both piers, the vessel type and any connection. Ask whether the ticket includes a hotel or airport transfer rather than assuming it does.
  3. Read the total and conditions before paying. Check whether baggage, transfers and any vehicle are included. We do not quote an inter-island fare here because a current route-specific fare was not confirmed from the pages read.
  4. Save the confirmation and follow its check-in instructions. As of November 2026, Lomprayah's terms require arrival at its office at least 60 minutes before departure. Allow additional time to reach the pier.
  5. Recheck before leaving your accommodation. Confirm the departure pier, service status and onward transfer. Keep booking details available offline.

Lomprayah also advertises office sales with cash and cards and asks passengers to bring ID or a passport. For an arrival through Samui Airport, compare the complete flight-to-pier connection rather than booking solely on the ferry's departure time. Our Koh Samui arrival guide covers the wider journey.

Luggage and bulky equipment

As of November 2026, Lomprayah's online terms give a large-luggage allowance of 20 kg and state an additional charge of THB 200 above that weight. Confirm how the charge applies to your bags before paying, especially with bulky equipment. Water-sports equipment has separate published charges, so do not assume the 20 kg allowance covers it. Treat this as Lomprayah's published policy, not a shared allowance across ferry companies.

We could not confirm a numerical allowance for Seatran Discovery or Songserm from the pages read. Ask your operator about each large bag, sports equipment or pushchair before booking. Songserm's own advice notes limited speedboat luggage space and recommends waterproof protection for valuables. As practical packing advice, keep documents, electronics and anything needed during the crossing in a small waterproof bag you can carry yourself.

Monsoon months and rough seas

For these Gulf islands, pay particular attention to October through December. The Thai Meteorological Department's Ko Samui station normals for 1991 to 2020 show these as its three wettest months. Those are Koh Samui rainfall observations, not separate measurements for Koh Phangan or Koh Tao and not a forecast of the sea on your travel day. See island weather and when to visit the Thai islands for broader planning.

The department's shipping forecast addresses winds, waves and thunderstorms in the Gulf. Songserm warns that high winds and rough seas can affect speedboat schedules and comfort, while Lomprayah's terms allow route and timetable changes because of weather. Check the current shipping forecast and the operator's service advice close to departure. Do not assume that a larger vehicle ferry is a guaranteed alternative when another service changes.

Our planning recommendation is to leave a spare night before an important flight rather than depending on a same-day crossing from Koh Tao or Koh Phangan. If disruption occurs, contact the company that issued your ticket before buying another one, and ask about the options for that booking. Keep accommodation plans flexible around the crossing.

Frequently asked questions

How long is Koh Samui to Koh Phangan by ferry?

As of November 2026, Seatran Discovery gives around 30 to 45 minutes from Bangrak to Thong Sala. For any direct Raja crossing from Lipa Noi, ask the company to confirm availability before comparing journey times. Choose by the actual departure offered and its pier.

Can I travel from Koh Phangan to Koh Tao?

Lomprayah lists that route and publishes a one-hour duration in its overview as of November 2026. Check date-specific departures, arrival details and baggage conditions before booking. Our island-hopping activity guide helps with the wider plan.

Does a Koh Samui ferry ticket always mean the same pier?

No. The operators list several Koh Samui piers. Check the precise departure location on your ticket and use that location for your transfer.

Should I buy the cheapest ticket I find?

Compare the complete booking first: departure pier, transfers, baggage and change conditions. A low headline fare is not enough information to arrange the journey. Confirm the total with the operating company for your date.

guides.title: Koh Samui vs Koh Phangan vs Koh Tao: Which to Choose?
guides.summary: Compare Koh Samui, Koh Phangan and Koh Tao for beaches, diving and easy arrivals, with suggested night splits and ferry planning for a first Gulf islands trip.
guides.html:
Koh Samui, Koh Phangan and Koh Tao are Gulf of Thailand islands that you can combine by ferry. Our recommendation is to choose Koh Samui for an arrival through its own airport and a varied beach holiday, Koh Phangan for beach days with the option of a retreat, and Koh Tao when diving or snorkelling is the reason for travelling. These are planning recommendations, rather than a ranking of which island is objectively best.

With a week, we would choose one island or two. With ten nights or more, consider all three, but count arrival, ferry and departure days before deciding how much beach time remains. Every suggested split below counts nights, including any return stay before flying out.

The three islands compared

IslandChoose it forIdeas for your stayAccess and trade-off
Koh SamuiOur first pick for a varied holiday with direct island air accessChaweng or Lamai beaches, cooking classes and Muay Thai trainingIts own airport; staying here alone avoids inter-island packing and transfers
Koh PhanganOur pick for combining beach days with yoga or meditationWest coast beaches, hills and a retreat; Haad Rin if the Full Moon Party interests youNo airport; include a boat journey in the arrival plan
Koh TaoOur pick for a holiday organised around diving and snorkellingSairee Beach, time underwater and a beach day without a dive bookingNo airport; allow a separate return transfer before an important flight

Koh Samui: start here for air access and variety

Samui Airport is on Koh Samui. If a boat transfer immediately after flying feels like too much, make Samui your first base. The island has beaches including Chaweng and Lamai, while cooking classes and Muay Thai offer ways to spend a day away from the sand. We recommend Samui for a first family trip if keeping the arrival simple matters more than visiting several islands.

Before choosing a room, compare Chaweng, Lamai and Bophut in our where to stay on Koh Samui guide. For a single-island holiday, use the five-day Samui itinerary as a starting point and leave gaps for beach time.

Koh Phangan: choose your beach, then your plans

Koh Phangan, also written Ko Pha-ngan in official tourism material, offers hills, beaches and yoga or meditation retreats. The Full Moon Party is associated with Haad Rin, but you need not make that event the purpose of your stay. For a beach-led visit, put the west coast's Haad Yao and Haad Salad on your shortlist.

We would give Phangan more nights than Samui if your ideal week involves settling into one beach base and leaving some days unplanned. If a retreat is the priority, check its actual programme and location before arranging ferries. Use where to stay on Koh Phangan to compare bases, and the Full Moon Party guide before making date-dependent bookings.

Koh Tao: give underwater plans enough space

Koh Tao is a diving and snorkelling destination, with Sairee Beach among its highlights. Choose it when time in the water matters more than a long checklist of land attractions. Non-divers can still build a stay around beaches, boat trips and walking. Read things to do on Koh Tao before deciding how much of your trip to spend here.

For a course, agree the programme with your instructor before allocating nights. Our learning to dive on Koh Tao guide explains the questions to ask. We recommend leaving spare time rather than assuming your arrival afternoon can count as a full training day. Check onward travel with your instructor too. This comparison does not set a course duration or a flying-after-diving interval.

Ferry links between the islands

As of November 2026, Lomprayah lists connections between Koh Samui and Koh Phangan, Koh Phangan and Koh Tao, and Koh Samui and Koh Tao. Use these listed routes to compare island combinations, then confirm the actual sailing for your date. Check intermediate stops and any need for an overnight stay before booking accommodation.

Do not arrange a taxi using the island name alone. Lomprayah lists several Samui departure points. As of November 2026, its website also carries a notice of temporary schedule and pier changes from 5 November to 5 December 2026. Confirm the exact boarding location and arrival pier for your sailing, even if an earlier search showed something different.

  • Samui and Phangan: our suggested pair when beach time is the priority and you want an arrival through Samui Airport.
  • Phangan and Tao: our suggested pair when you want a beach stay followed by time devoted to diving or snorkelling.
  • Samui and Tao: our suggested pair when diving is important but you do not want three accommodation bases.

Use the Samui, Phangan and Tao ferry guide and island hopping by ferry page for the next planning step. Confirm fares, departure times, baggage conditions and transfers with the operating company for your travel date. We give no fixed crossing time or fare here.

How to split seven, ten or fourteen nights

These are our suggested allocations, not package itineraries or minimum stays. They assume arrival and departure through Samui Airport. The final Samui night is a planning buffer, not a guarantee against disruption.

Available nightsSuggested splitWhy we suggest it
Seven, beach focusSamui 3, Phangan 3, Samui 1Two islands with time to settle into each; the last night puts you back on the airport island
Seven, diving focusSamui 2, Tao 4, Samui 1Gives Tao the larger share; confirm that your chosen dive programme and onward travel fit
Ten, all threeSamui 3, Phangan 3, Tao 3, Samui 1A balanced introduction, provided you accept several transfer days
Fourteen, slower paceSamui 4, Phangan 5, Tao 4, Samui 1More room for unplanned days; swap a Phangan night to Tao if diving is your priority

For fewer than seven nights, our preference is a single base. If you have ten days rather than ten nights, recount your accommodation nights before copying the table. The ten-day island-hopping itinerary is a separate day-by-day planning option.

Costs and connections to compare before booking

Price the complete journey for your dates: accommodation, transport to each pier, boat tickets and transport after landing. Add the actual activities you want, especially a dive programme, rather than assuming one island will always be cheaper. A room saving can be less useful if it adds transfers you would prefer to avoid.

Koh Phangan and Koh Tao have no airport. If your flight leaves from Samui, we recommend returning there before departure day rather than relying on a boat and flight connection on the same day. Check current operator notices before each move. For seasonal planning, use the best time to visit the Thai islands and weather pages.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which island should I choose for a first visit?

We suggest Samui if arriving through an island airport and having different activities available are your priorities. Choose Phangan for a beach-and-retreat plan, or Tao if diving is the main reason for the trip.

Can I visit all three islands in a week?

The ferry network connects them, but we recommend choosing two for seven nights. Packing, getting to piers and checking into new accommodation all take space out of a short holiday.

Is Koh Phangan worth visiting without the Full Moon Party?

Yes, in our view. Plan around its beaches, hills or retreats instead. Choose your base for those activities and consult the party guide if you want to avoid planning around an event night.

Is Koh Tao only for divers?

No. Snorkelling, beaches, boat trips and walking are alternatives. We would still give Tao the most nights when underwater activities are your main interest.

Do I need to return to Samui after Koh Tao?

Only if your onward arrangements require it. Lomprayah also lists mainland connections. Choose your exit route before booking the island stays, and include the full journey to your next destination.

guides.title: Koh Samui vs Phuket: Which Island Fits Your Trip?
guides.summary: Choose between Koh Samui and Phuket with a comparison of their different rainy seasons, airport access, beach bases, spending decisions and excursions.
guides.html:
Koh Samui is in the Gulf of Thailand; Phuket is on the Andaman Sea. For a first island holiday, choose by travel month before comparing hotel photographs. Our recommendation is Koh Samui for a beach-focused stay with an Ang Thong excursion, and Phuket if your wish list centres on Patong nightlife or an outing towards Phi Phi. Neither island wins every category.

Koh Samui and Phuket at a glance

DecisionKoh SamuiPhuket
Rainfall pattern (TMD 1991 to 2020 station normals)Ko Samui (48550): wettest October to DecemberPhuket (48564): wetter May to October
AirportSamui Airport (USM)Phuket International Airport (HKT)
Beach shortlistChaweng and LamaiKata, Karon and Kamala
Family starting pointCompare a beach stay with a Bophut village baseCompare Kata with quieter northern beaches
Evening starting pointChaweng for beach partiesPatong for bars and nightlife
Excursion shortlistAng Thong National Marine ParkPhang Nga Bay or Phi Phi
Budget decisionPrice flights and the beach base togetherPrice flights and the beach base together

Season: use the correct coast's calendar

The Thai Meteorological Department's 1991 to 2020 normals for Ko Samui station (48550) put the largest monthly rainfall totals in October to December, peaking in November. Phuket station (48564), not Phuket Airport station, records its wetter stretch from May to October, with September the wettest month. These are station averages, not forecasts for your beach.

Our weather-based recommendation is to compare both for February and March, lean towards Koh Samui for July or August, and favour Phuket over Samui for a November beach trip. December still needs care on Samui. Keep boat days flexible. See the best time to visit the Thai islands and check the weather before departure.

Access and flights: compare the complete journey

Bangkok Airways lists direct flights from Bangkok Suvarnabhumi (BKK) to both Samui Airport and Phuket International Airport. It also lists a direct Samui to Phuket route. Check the operating airline's booking page for your dates, rather than treating a route listing as confirmation of a particular departure. No fare or flight frequency is assumed here.

For Koh Samui, choose flights into USM if avoiding a ferry connection is a priority. The airline lists taxis and airport minivan transfers for reaching Chaweng, Lamai and other parts of the island. Our Koh Samui access guide explains the alternatives, including Surat Thani Airport. Compare the whole transfer before deciding that an alternative airport is better value.

For Phuket, compare an itinerary ending at HKT with the cost of continuing to Samui. Check your own departure city for available international services, rather than assuming either island has a non-stop flight from home. Bangkok Airways lists taxis, airport shuttles and public buses among Phuket's onward options. Ask for a transfer quote to your actual accommodation, not just to the island.

Beaches: choose a base before choosing an island

On Koh Samui, start with Chaweng Beach and Lamai Beach, both highlighted by the Tourism Authority of Thailand. Visit the area guides for Chaweng and Chaweng Noi and Lamai to decide where to sleep. For a stay with village character, compare Bophut, where TAT describes converted Chinese shophouses. Do not assume a village base and your preferred swimming beach are the same thing.

On Phuket, compare Kata, Karon and Kamala rather than choosing Patong by default. TAT identifies Kata as a family option and describes northern beaches as quieter than the south. Our Phuket overview is the starting point for this island. For either choice, check the accommodation's exact beach access and the day's sea conditions. For swimming, follow local warnings and red flags, as the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office advises. Check conditions at the beach before entering the water.

Families versus nightlife

For families, we would shortlist Bophut on Samui if the village setting appeals, then compare it with a beach-based stay. On Phuket, start with Kata if you want a recognised family beach base, or investigate the north if quiet matters more. Choose the room location as carefully as the resort area: ask about evening music, the walk to meals and whether reaching the sand means crossing a road.

For nightlife, Chaweng has beach parties, while Patong has bars and nightlife. Our recommendation is Phuket if Patong itself is part of the appeal; choose Chaweng if you want evenings out within a Samui holiday. Families do not need to reject either whole island because of its party areas, and couples need not book beside those areas to enjoy dinner out. Use where to stay on Koh Samui to narrow the decision.

Costs in general terms

We do not rank one island as universally cheaper. Build two quotes for the same dates and standard of room, then add baggage, airport transfers, meals and the excursions you actually want. Compare the final total for everyone travelling. A room-only comparison leaves too much of the decision out.

For a restrained budget, prioritise a base that reduces paid journeys and choose which boat outing matters most before booking it. Ask what an excursion includes, especially accommodation pickup, meals and park admission. Compare cancellation terms as well as the headline price. These are budgeting recommendations, not a price survey or a promise of savings.

Day trips: Ang Thong or the Andaman islands?

For Koh Samui, Mu Ko Ang Thong National Park is the excursion to put on the shortlist. TAT describes it as a day trip from Samui and highlights kayaking. Read our Ang Thong day-trip guide before choosing an outing. Check current park access and the marine forecast before paying.

From Phuket, TAT lists day tours to Phang Nga Bay and Koh Phi Phi. Pick the destination you most want to see rather than the longest list of stops. Check the day's operating conditions and the exact landing itinerary. For a day without a boat, Phuket's Old Town is another option. We recommend keeping a spare day for an excursion instead of making it the only reason for a short stay.

Who should pick which?

  • Pick Koh Samui if a beach base, Bophut's village setting and an Ang Thong outing match your plans. Start with the five-day Koh Samui itinerary.
  • Pick Phuket if Kata, Patong or an Andaman day trip is central to your holiday, and your flight itinerary works well into HKT.
  • Let the month break a tie. Use the coast-specific climate comparison above before committing to a non-refundable beach stay.
  • For a short holiday, pick one. We would spend the time settling into a base rather than changing islands simply to tick both off.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Koh Samui or Phuket better for a first visit?

Our pick depends on the trip: Koh Samui for a beach stay with Ang Thong on the shortlist, Phuket for Kata, Patong or an Andaman excursion. Compare your travel month and complete flight cost before making the final choice.

Which island is better with children?

Compare specific accommodation rather than awarding an island-wide winner. We suggest starting with Bophut or a beach base on Samui, and Kata on Phuket. Check walking routes, room noise and beach conditions before booking.

Is Phuket always cheaper than Koh Samui?

No blanket price ranking is established here. Get comparable quotes including flights and transfers. Your chosen room and daily travel plans belong in the comparison, along with any boat trips.

Can I visit both in one holiday?

Bangkok Airways lists a direct Samui to Phuket flight. Treat a two-island stay as an itinerary choice with a travel day, not a day trip. Our two-week Thai islands itinerary can help you decide whether changing coasts fits your plans.

guides.title: Learning to Dive on Koh Tao: PADI or SSI?
guides.summary: Compare PADI and SSI Open Water courses on Koh Tao, check age and medical rules, choose a school and plan the no-fly interval and insurance before booking.
guides.html:
Planning to learn to dive on Koh Tao in Thailand? Start with the full Open Water Diver course and compare the actual teaching arrangements before choosing PADI or SSI. Ask for the course schedule, medical form and complete price in writing. Keep your flight plans flexible until you know when the final dive is scheduled.

This guide uses PADI, SSI, Divers Alert Network (DAN) and UK government guidance checked in November 2026. It does not rank schools or quote an island-wide course price. Use it alongside our scuba-diving overview and Gulf island ferry guide when planning the trip.

PADI versus SSI: compare the course you will actually take

PADI and SSI both offer Open Water Diver training. PADI describes a progression through theory, confined-water practice and open-water dives. SSI combines academic learning with confined-water and open-water sessions. Do not choose solely by the agency logo: ask who will teach you, how many learners share that instructor and what happens if you need more practice.

QuestionPADISSI
Minimum starting age10 in most areas; under-15s earn Junior Open Water Diver certification10; ask for the age-specific junior restrictions
Open-water trainingFour open-water divesAt least four open-water training dives
Published durationAdvertised as possible in as little as 2 to 4 daysSuggested training duration of 16 to 32 hours
Studying before arrivaleLearning can cover the knowledge-development portion before travellingDigital learning is available through the SSI app
What to confirm in the quoteLearning materials, water training, equipment hire and certificationDigital kit, tuition, water training and certification

These are agency descriptions, not a promise about a particular Koh Tao timetable. Ask for the exact qualification name. If a cheaper offer is a try-dive experience, do not treat it as the full Open Water Diver course. PADI describes Discover Scuba Diving as a supervised opportunity to try diving before enrolling in certification training.

Age and water confidence

The starting age is not a recommendation that every child should enrol. Discuss your child's confidence, equipment fit and attention span with the instructor before paying. Ask for the applicable junior depth and buddy restrictions in writing rather than applying adult limits to a child. SSI requires a parent or guardian to review and sign a minor's training forms.

PADI assesses basic swimming and floating skills; SSI requires a water-fitness evaluation including a swim assessment and survival float before open-water training. Ask the school to explain its assessment before booking. If swimming itself feels stressful, allow time to work on that before adding scuba equipment.

Read the medical questionnaire before travelling

Request the current Diver Medical Participant Questionnaire early. Complete it honestly and follow its branching instructions. The 2026 form says an all-No response to its ten initial questions does not require a medical evaluation under that screening form. PADI also notes that local laws in some areas require a physician consultation for all students, so confirm any additional requirements before booking. Certain Yes answers require follow-up questions or a physician's evaluation. A Yes is a reason to follow the form, not to change the answer to secure a place.

If the form directs you to a physician, take all three pages, including the physician's evaluation page, and arrange the assessment before your water training. Consult your physician if you have a fitness concern the questionnaire does not cover. Do not rely on a school salesperson to decide medical fitness. SSI also lists a medical questionnaire or physician's approval where required among its training paperwork.

How many days should you allow on Koh Tao?

For planning, reserve four course days plus a spare day, then add your no-fly interval after the actual final dive. This is our suggested buffer, not a local course standard. PADI's short advertised duration and SSI's training-hour range do not guarantee that you will finish on a particular afternoon.

Ask for a day-by-day outline showing study, confined-water practice and the open-water dives. Check whether study must be completed before arrival and what extra tuition costs if you need it. Completing theory beforehand can free up holiday time, but does not replace water training. If you already have documented training from home, arrange a referral with both centres before travelling.

Avoid making your course the last tightly scheduled stop of an island-hopping trip. Put a flexible stay or quiet day after it. Use our Koh Tao planning guide for the rest of your visit rather than adding another dive merely to fill that buffer.

Questions to ask a school before paying

  • Credentials and teaching. Ask to see the operator's credentials and confirm the instructor's qualifications. What language will instruction use? How many students will share the instructor, and can you meet them before committing?
  • Practice time. Where will confined-water training happen? What happens if you cannot complete a skill that day? Ask about extra sessions, charges and rescheduling rather than accepting a guaranteed finish date.
  • Equipment. Check the condition and fit of the equipment you will use. Ask what hire is included and how the school handles a fault during training.
  • Emergency arrangements. Ask to see the boat's oxygen provision. Who can administer it? How would the team call for help at sea and transfer a diver to a hyperbaric chamber?
  • Written inclusions. Get one total covering learning materials, equipment hire, tuition, training dives and certification. Ask separately about transport, medical assessment, cancellation and any included insurance.

The UK government's Thailand advice specifically recommends checking operator credentials, equipment condition, oxygen and chamber-transfer arrangements. Treat vague answers as a reason to keep looking. A low price alone tells you little about the time and support you will receive.

No-fly time: count from surfacing after the last dive

DAN's published guidance for divers without decompression-sickness symptoms gives these minimum preflight surface intervals for recreational air diving:

Dive historyDAN recommendation
One no-decompression diveAt least 12 hours
Multiple dives in a day or diving over multiple days, within no-decompression limitsAt least 18 hours
Dives requiring decompression stopsSubstantially longer than 18 hours; obtain appropriate advice

For repeated course dives within no-decompression limits, use the multiple-dive category. Count from the end of the actual last dive, including any optional dive you add afterwards. For example, finishing at 16:00 means an 18-hour minimum ends at 10:00 the next day. A transfer journey does not restart or shorten that clock.

For itinerary planning, leave at least a full 24-hour buffer before your flight, and longer if your instructor or dive computer requires it. That buffer is our planning recommendation. DAN says longer intervals reduce risk, but its minimums do not guarantee avoidance of decompression sickness. Its guidance applies to cabin altitudes of 2,000 to 8,000 feet, so do not assume a short flight needs a shorter wait.

If you develop signs or symptoms that might indicate decompression sickness, seek medical advice and do not fly. Waiting out a countdown is not medical clearance. Keep our emergency contacts accessible and ask the instructor how to obtain diving medical help before your first boat trip.

Insurance: get confirmation for a beginner course

Before paying, ask your insurer to confirm in writing that your policy covers an uncertified learner taking an instructor-led Open Water Diver course in Thailand. Give the course dates and planned activities. Ask about permitted depths, instructor qualifications and any medical declarations. The UK government's advice notes that some policies require particular instructor qualifications.

Ask explicitly about dive-accident treatment, recompression treatment, emergency evacuation and repatriation. Request the limits, excess and emergency contact procedure. If the school includes insurance, ask for the policy wording and whose costs it covers. Do not infer personal medical cover from an operator saying it is insured. This checklist does not establish cover under any individual policy.

Before you book

Get the exact qualification, instructor arrangements, full quote and medical paperwork first. Then reserve enough time for training, a spare day and a flight buffer. Fit your course around the wider Koh Samui, Koh Phangan and Koh Tao trip, with the final dive time written next to your onward flight time.

guides.title: Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC): Free Official Form
guides.summary: Prepare Thailand's free TDAC for a Koh Samui, Koh Phangan or Koh Tao trip. Check the official address, submission window and tourist stays by nationality.
guides.html:
Planning Koh Samui, Koh Phangan or Koh Tao? Put the Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC) on your pre-departure checklist. It is an online arrival form, separate from a visa. Official sources below were checked on 16 November 2026.

The official TDAC website and cost

Type https://tdac.immigration.go.th directly into your browser. As of November 2026, the official TDAC is free of charge. Do not pay a registration fee.

The Ministry of Tourism and Sports warns about fake TDAC websites charging travellers. A similar name or official-looking design is no reason to trust a page. Check the exact address before entering passport details, and leave a page that asks you to pay for TDAC registration.

Who must complete it?

Non-Thai nationals entering Thailand by air, land or sea need a TDAC. That includes tourists and long-term residents. Visa-exempt visitors still need the form, and children and infants need their own entries.

Travellers transferring without passing through Thai immigration and people entering with a Border Pass are exceptions. Immigration's FAQ also exempts crew. If your connection involves entering Thailand through immigration, treat it as an arrival.

When to submit: within three days of arrival

The Immigration Bureau FAQ says to submit within three days before arriving, including the arrival date. Use your arrival in Thailand when planning the submission, rather than your departure from home. Complete it before entry and follow the official form's available arrival dates.

Submit a new TDAC each time you enter Thailand. Do not reuse one from an earlier visit.

What details does TDAC ask for?

Have these ready before opening the form:

  • Your passport and personal details.
  • Travel information, including your arrival date, flight number if flying, and purpose of travel.
  • Your accommodation address in Thailand.
  • Health declaration information requested by the form.
  • An email address to receive your TDAC.

Enter details in English. Review the preview before submitting, then download the arrival card and keep it accessible for the journey. The official manual provides an Update Arrival Card option for correcting submitted information before travel. Full name, passport number, nationality and date of birth cannot be updated through that option. For corrections to information that cannot be updated, Immigration's FAQ recommends submitting a new form with the correct details.

Tourist visa exemption by passport nationality

As of November 2026, the MFA's published chart for ordinary passport holders gives the following tourist visa exemption periods. Its revised scheme took effect on 15 September 2026; the MFA says the former 60-day scheme was revoked. These are tourist exemption periods, subject to immigration requirements, rather than permission conferred by TDAC.

Ordinary passport nationalityPublished tourist exemption
United KingdomUp to 30 days
United StatesUp to 30 days
AustraliaUp to 30 days
Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, SwedenUp to 30 days for each listed nationality

The European nationalities are listed individually so you can match your passport to the official chart. Recheck the MFA or Immigration Bureau before departure. For a longer stay or another purpose, check the appropriate visa requirements before booking around an assumed exemption. See our visa planning page.

Fit the paperwork around your island trip

Keep your arrival details and accommodation address alongside your Koh Samui travel plan. Use the Samui, Phangan and Tao ferry guide for the next stage of your itinerary, and transport planning to organise the wider journey.

guides.title: Thailand Public Holidays 2027: Island Travel Calendar
guides.summary: Plan Koh Samui, Koh Phangan and Koh Tao trips around Thailand’s 2027 bank holidays, Buddhist alcohol restrictions and dates to recheck before island travel.
guides.html:
Thailand holidays for Koh Samui, Koh Phangan and Koh Tao

Use this calendar when planning a trip to Koh Samui, Koh Phangan or Koh Tao. It reproduces the Bank of Thailand's 18 listed financial-institution holidays for 2027, checked on 16 November 2026. The notification identifies the year as B.E. 2570 (2027).

This is the bank calendar. It is a confirmed planning reference, rather than a complete calendar for government offices or every employer. Do not use it alone to decide when an immigration office, shop or attraction will close. A separate nationwide Cabinet calendar for 2027 was not confirmed in this review.

Official Bank of Thailand holiday calendar, 2027

The notification provides conditional additional holidays for Islamic Bank of Thailand and for bank branches in Narathiwat, Pattani, Yala, Satun and Songkhla. Check the individual branch calendar separately before arranging counter services in these provinces.

Which holidays bring alcohol sale restrictions?

As of November 2026, the government lists five restricted-sale Buddhist observances: Makha Bucha, Visakha Bucha, Asalha Bucha, Khao Phansa (beginning of Buddhist Lent) and Ok Phansa (end of Buddhist Lent). Exemptions apply to qualifying international-flight airport passenger buildings, entertainment venues licensed under the Entertainment Place Act, hotels under the Hotel Act, establishments operating similarly to entertainment venues in tourist areas designated by the Ministry of Public Health, and venues hosting qualifying national or international events designated by that ministry. Ask the venue to confirm eligibility and current conditions.

The bank calendar confirms Makha Bucha on Sunday 21 February, Visakha Bucha on Thursday 20 May and Asarnha Bucha on Sunday 18 July 2027. These observances are distinct from substitute bank holidays. Exact 2027 Khao Phansa and Ok Phansa dates were not confirmed from an official calendar in this review.

The government requires safeguards at exempt establishments. Recheck the current rule before planning an evening out; an island address alone does not establish an exemption. See Makha Bucha and Visakha Bucha for context.

Long weekends and dates worth planning around

Combining Saturdays and Sundays with the bank calendar gives these breaks. These are calendar calculations, not a guarantee that a business closes throughout.

  • 1 to 3 January: New Year and the weekend.
  • 20 to 22 February: the weekend and Monday's Makha Bucha substitute.
  • 13 to 15 April: Songkran falls Tuesday to Thursday. The bank list does not add 12 or 16 April.
  • 1 to 4 May: the weekend, Labour Day substitute and Coronation Day.
  • 17 to 19 July: the weekend and Monday's Asarnha Bucha substitute.
  • 23 to 25 October: the weekend and Monday's Chulalongkorn substitute.
  • 4 to 6 December: the weekend and Monday's substitute holiday.
  • 10 to 12 December: Constitution Day and the weekend.
  • 31 December to 2 January 2028: New Year's Eve and the following weekend. The 2028 substitute calendar is outside this guide.

Treat extra bridge days as unconfirmed until an official announcement includes them. A Thursday holiday also deserves an availability check if your trip depends on a particular flight or sailing.

What closes on the islands?

  • Bank counter services: plan around the listed bank holidays and check the individual branch before travelling there. The notification concerns financial institutions, not a blanket shutdown of island businesses.
  • Government and immigration offices: check the office's own holiday notice before planning paperwork. Allow a working-day buffer instead of assuming its calendar matches the bank list.
  • Shops, restaurants and accommodation: ask the business about the date you need. No island-wide 2027 closure schedule for these services was confirmed.
  • Ferries, flights and excursions: check the operator's date-specific availability. Secure the transfer before committing to a tight connection. See the Samui, Phangan and Tao ferry guide and how to get to Koh Samui.
  • Alcohol retailers and nightlife: check the Buddhist observance date and current rules separately from opening hours.

What gets crowded, and how should you book?

Songkran and New Year deserve early transport checks. A ferry operator's 2015 annual report identifies long holidays, including New Year and Songkran, as a source of seasonal demand. This is historical evidence, not a forecast of 2027 passenger numbers or sold-out sailings. TAT also advised advance travel planning in its 2026 Songkran announcement.

For Koh Samui, confirm arrival and departure transport before fixing non-refundable accommodation. For Koh Phangan and Koh Tao, secure every ferry leg and allow time for onward connections. Check both directions around long weekends. Use the Full Moon Party guide separately when planning Koh Phangan dates.

For a quieter stay, ask your accommodation about local celebration areas before choosing a room. Specific 2027 street-event programmes and crowd hotspots on Koh Samui, Koh Phangan and Koh Tao were not confirmed in this review. Consult the Songkran page for festival context and recheck local announcements before travelling.

Comparing coasts? Start with which Thai island is best. A national holiday alone does not establish opening arrangements or crowd levels on Phuket, Koh Lanta or Koh Chang.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many bank holidays does Thailand have in 2027?

The Bank of Thailand lists 18 nationwide financial-institution holidays, including all three Songkran days, with additional provisions for specified institutions and southern branches.

Is Songkran a five-day bank holiday in 2027?

The verified list includes Tuesday 13, Wednesday 14 and Thursday 15 April. It does not include Monday 12 or Friday 16 April. Recheck for later official additions.

Does a substitute bank holiday move the Buddhist observance?

The calendar distinguishes them: Makha Bucha is Sunday 21 February, with the substitute bank holiday on Monday 22 February. Asarnha Bucha is Sunday 18 July, with the bank holiday on Monday 19 July.

Will a holiday cancel my island ferry?

This calendar does not establish ferry operations. Confirm the sailing with the operator for your travel date and leave time for the onward journey.
