guides.budget: Confirm date-specific transport and accommodation quotes before committing to a holiday trip

guides.title: Things to Do in Koh Phangan Beyond the Full Moon Party
guides.summary: Koh Phangan offers beach days, snorkelling around Koh Ma, forest outings and yoga. Pick a coast for each day and leave room to change plans with the weather.
guides.html:
Koh Phangan, officially romanised Ko Pha-ngan, is an island in Surat Thani province in the Gulf of Thailand. Its hills, waterfalls and beaches give you plenty to build a holiday around beyond the Full Moon Party. Start with one beach outing and one inland outing, then add activities that interest you. The suggestions below are intended as a flexible plan, rather than a list to complete.

Spend a day on the west coast

Make Haad Yao your choice for a beach afternoon that ends with sunset. The government tourism guide specifically recommends its sunset views. Bring a book and resist the temptation to leave as soon as you have taken a photograph. For another beach outing, consider Haad Salad, which the same guide identifies as a snorkelling spot. Choose between them for a longer stop instead of trying to squeeze both into a short visit.

Use our Srithanu and west coast guide to organise this part of the trip. If a yoga class is your priority, book that first and fit the beach around it. Do not schedule a class immediately after an outing with an uncertain return time.

See the Koh Ma sandbar and consider snorkelling

Mae Haad Beach is connected to Koh Ma by a sandbar exposed at low tide. Come to see the connection between beach and islet, without assuming the crossing will be exposed when you arrive. Ask locally about the tide and crossing conditions before setting off; do not cross if conditions are unsuitable.

The Tourism Authority of Thailand describes Koh Ma as a shallow snorkelling spot. For a first attempt, read our snorkelling guide and ask locally about an appropriate entry point and the day's sea conditions. Treat a beach recommendation as a starting point for planning, rather than a promise of safe water or clear visibility. Leave coral untouched and keep the outing within your swimming ability.

Give Bottle Beach its own outing

Bottle Beach lies on the north of Koh Phangan. The Tourism Authority of Thailand's 2018 brochure describes access by taxi boat or forest trail; confirm the current options locally before choosing either. Choose how you will get there and back before leaving, particularly if you are considering a boat. Ask where the return departs, what happens if conditions change, and how you will contact the person arranging it.

Do not treat the beach and Bottle Beach Viewpoint as interchangeable stops. If you want to add the viewpoint, check the current approach and conditions separately. A beach day is a complete outing on its own. Leave the climb for another day if anyone in your group is unsure.

Explore waterfalls without committing to a summit

Access check, 16 November 2026: DNP lists all Than Sadet-Ko Pha-ngan National Park tourist sites and accommodation temporarily closed from 12 November onwards due to heavy rain, with no reopening date. Confirm a reopening notice with the park before planning a waterfall visit or entering a park trail.

Start your inland planning with Than Sadet Ko Pha-ngan National Park. Phaeng Waterfall has several tiers; Than Sadet Waterfall is another option described in the official provincial tourism brochure. Pick one waterfall outing first, then ask park staff which paths are open and suitable that day. Confirm current admission arrangements before travelling. Follow warning signs at the coast and take care near waterfalls, as UK travel advice recommends.

For a more ambitious walk, research Khao Ra through the hiking guide. Do not infer that a trail is open from its appearance in an older brochure. Ask about access and a guide before making it the centre of your day. Ask park staff what to carry, what footwear the route needs and when to turn back. Follow their advice and any closure notices.

Make time for yoga

If you want to practise yoga in Srithanu on Koh Phangan, check availability directly before planning around a class. Start with our yoga and wellness guide, then ask a prospective teacher about the class style, experience expected and any adjustments you need. Try a single class before committing to a longer programme. Check the current schedule directly, since an advertised studio does not necessarily have group classes running during your stay.

A class can be the day's main activity. Keep the remaining time free for lunch and a beach stop instead of adding an early hike and a late boat trip around it.

Plan an easy day at Thong Nai Pan

Use the Thong Nai Pan area guide and Thong Nai Pan Noi beach page to plan a day devoted to this part of Koh Phangan. The official provincial brochure describes Thong Nai Pan as a crescent bay. Choose it as an alternative beach day, rather than adding it after Bottle Beach and a waterfall.

For families, our suggestion is to keep the plan simple: one beach, a meal break and a return arranged before everyone is tired. Check conditions at the water's edge together. If the sea does not suit your group, change the activity rather than searching for a way to make the original plan work.

Arrange arrival and choose a base

Koh Phangan has no airport. Plan the boat leg as part of your arrival, using the Samui, Phangan and Tao ferry guide. Thong Sala has a passenger pier; our Thong Sala and Baan Tai guide is a useful starting point for arrival planning. Confirm the exact pier on your ticket before arranging onward transport.

Choose accommodation around the days you most want to have. Read where to stay in Koh Phangan before booking, and keep travel to activities in mind. If you also want to visit Haad Rin, give it a separate place in your plan. Our Full Moon Party guide handles party planning.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many days should I allow on Koh Phangan?

We suggest four days as a starting plan: a west coast day, a waterfall outing, another beach day and some unallocated time. The Koh Phangan four-day itinerary helps you organise those choices. This is an editorial recommendation, not a minimum stay.

What should I prioritise if I do not want to party?

Choose Haad Yao for sunset, Mae Haad for the Koh Ma sandbar, and either a waterfall outing or a yoga class. Add Bottle Beach if arranging the access appeals to you. You do not need to include Haad Rin to make the trip worthwhile.

Can I book a fixed programme before arriving?

Book the essentials, but keep outdoor days flexible. Check park access, sea conditions and class availability close to the visit. Use the weather page when deciding which outing to do next.
guides.bestTime: Choose outdoor days around current weather, sea conditions and park access
guides.budget: Flexible: confirm transport, park admission and activity costs before booking

guides.title: Things to Do in Koh Samui: Beaches, Temples and Ang Thong
guides.summary: Plan things to do on Koh Samui: compare beaches, pair temple visits, explore inland waterfalls and choose an Ang Thong day trip, with ideas for rainy days.
guides.html:
On Koh Samui, also written Ko Samui, build your holiday around the things you want time to enjoy. We suggest a beach day, a temple outing and a separate day for Ang Thong, rather than a different excursion every morning. Use this guide to choose your priorities, then turn them into a route with our five-day Koh Samui itinerary. The days suggested here are planning choices, not a minimum stay.

Access check, November 2026: DNP lists all Ang Thong tourist sites and accommodation closed annually from 1 November to 15 December. Choose another outing during that period and confirm reopening before booking.

Choose a beach day first

Begin with one beach rather than trying to compare them all from a car window. Keep a second option for another day, and check conditions at the shore before deciding to swim.

  • Chaweng Beach. This east-coast beach has restaurants and shops along Chaweng Beach Road. Choose it if you want to combine sand time with a meal and some browsing. Our Chaweng and Chaweng Noi guide helps you plan the wider area.
  • Lamai Beach. South of Chaweng, Lamai also has places to eat and shops. Make it the focus of a day in Lamai rather than an extra stop after a long outing.
  • Silver Beach. This cove sits between Chaweng and Lamai. Consider it as an alternative to either of the longer beach days, rather than promising yourself all three.
  • Maenam Beach. A long sandy shore offers another option for a walk. Explore the wider Maenam and north coast area on a separate outing.

For a short stay, choose your base before choosing daily excursions. Read where to stay on Koh Samui and prioritise the beach you want to return to, rather than moving accommodation to tick off every shore.

Visit the Big Buddha and Wat Plai Laem

Big Buddha Temple, Wat Phra Yai, stands on Fan Island, connected to Koh Samui. Its golden Buddha is the main sight; stairs lead up to a viewing terrace. Allow time to look around rather than treating the temple as a photo stop on the way elsewhere.

Pair it in your plans with Wat Plai Laem, where large Guanyin and Budai figures appear above the water. The contrast makes this our suggested temple outing. Ask about access to worship areas when you arrive, follow the instructions displayed and give people praying space. Avoid packing the same day with a boat excursion.

Spend an evening in Bophut

Bophut and Fisherman's Village has converted Chinese shophouses. Set aside an evening to walk and choose somewhere to eat, with Fisherman's Village Walking Street as your starting point for planning. Check the current market arrangements locally before choosing a particular night: this guide does not promise a weekly schedule.

Keep the evening flexible. If you are travelling with children, agree on a meal stop before browsing; if you want a quieter outing, make the walk itself the plan rather than booking another activity afterwards.

Head inland for waterfalls and sculpture

  • Na Muang Waterfalls. The government tourism directory describes Na Muang's water flowing over granite. Choose it for a change from the coast, but decide how far to walk after checking the conditions and local advice. Do not build the visit around a promised swim.
  • Hin Lad Waterfall. Its jungle trail makes this a walking choice. Read the hiking guide, take suitable footwear and turn back if the route is beyond your group's comfort level.
  • Secret Buddha Garden. Stone sculptures are the reason to add this inland stop. Ask your transport provider to explain the access and return arrangements before agreeing to the journey.

Choose one inland focus for a half-day in your draft itinerary. Keep extra stops optional and leave time for lunch. This is especially useful if your group includes people who would rather sit on a beach than walk.

Add a coastal viewpoint or the Lamai rocks

Lad Koh Viewpoint is on the high road between Chaweng and Lamai. Consider a stop when planning a journey between those areas. The Hin Ta and Hin Yai rocks are another coastal sightseeing option. Choose whichever interests you, rather than treating both as compulsory additions to a beach day.

Give Ang Thong its own day

Mu Ko Ang Thong National Park is a separate island excursion from Koh Samui. The Tourism Authority of Thailand describes snorkelling and hiking, views of the Emerald Lake on Mae Ko, and sea kayaking around Sam Sao. These are possible interests to compare when choosing a trip, not a promise that every boat visits every stop.

Use our Ang Thong day-trip guide to decide what matters most. Before paying, ask for the exact itinerary, the walking involved, which activities are included and what happens if the sailing is cancelled. Check current national park notices for access and closures. Keep this day movable within your stay and have a land-based alternative.

If paddling matters more than a viewpoint, read kayaking and paddleboarding before comparing trips. For time in the water, start with the snorkelling guide. Avoid choosing solely by the number of stops advertised.

Try a class instead of another sightseeing circuit

The Tourism Authority of Thailand lists cooking courses, yoga, Muay Thai training and scuba diving among Koh Samui's activities. A Thai cooking class is our suggested change of pace after several beach days. Ask about the dishes, dietary requirements and how much cooking you will do yourself before booking.

For a more active session, explore Muay Thai training and explain your experience level when enquiring. If you prefer a slower day, compare yoga and wellness options. For scuba diving, ask the provider about training requirements and the actual dive location rather than assuming every trip stays close to Koh Samui.

Rainy days and family plans

Keep an indoor option in reserve. Ask a cooking-class provider whether the session is covered, and confirm availability before setting off. A yoga session may be another option if its venue suits the weather. Do not assume an outdoor temple, waterfall or boat outing becomes a good rainy-day substitute simply because it is away from the beach.

With children, our suggested starting point is one beach outing and one short sightseeing visit on separate days. Ask boat providers about the individual child's age, swimming ability and the demands of the advertised activities. See weather before deciding which plans to keep flexible.

Getting between your chosen stops

Group your plans by area, confirm the return journey and ask for a transport quote before you set off. Read transportation before choosing how to travel around the island. For arrival planning, use how to get to Koh Samui. Keep departure day free of an excursion with an uncertain return time.

Frequently Asked Questions

What should I prioritise on a first visit to Koh Samui?

Our suggested starting point is a beach day, the Big Buddha and Wat Plai Laem, then an Ang Thong excursion if access and sailing conditions allow. Add an inland visit only if it fits the pace you enjoy.

How many days should I allow for Koh Samui?

We suggest five days as a planning framework, with time for rest between outings. Our five-day itinerary offers a starting point; shorten the sightseeing list if you prefer longer beach days.

Is Ang Thong on Koh Samui?

No. It is a separate marine national park visited on trips from Koh Samui. Set aside a day in your plans, check current access and compare the actual activities included before booking.

What can I do on Koh Samui without a boat trip?

Choose beaches, the temples, an evening in Bophut or an inland outing. A cooking class or Muay Thai session offers a different kind of day. Confirm individual arrangements before travelling to a venue.

Can I combine everything in one day?

We do not recommend planning that way. Choose either a land-based outing or an Ang Thong excursion, and save beach time for its own day. You can then drop an optional stop without losing the main experience you came for.
guides.bestTime: Choose outdoor days using the local forecast and current park notices
guides.duration: 5 days suggested; adjust for beach time
guides.budget: Moderate; plan separately for transport, classes and boat excursions

guides.title: Things to Do in Koh Tao for Divers and Non-Divers
guides.summary: Plan Koh Tao diving, snorkelling, beach days and viewpoint walks, with Koh Nang Yuan boat trips and flexible ideas for friends choosing different activities.
guides.html:
Koh Tao, also written Ko Tao, rewards a plan that leaves room for both water and land. Scuba diving is a reason to come, but the Tourism Authority of Thailand also recommends boat trips, hiking and yoga for non-divers. Start by deciding how much of your stay you want to spend underwater. A mixed group need not book the same activities every day: let divers organise their training or boat dives, then arrange to meet for a meal or an evening on Sairee Beach.

Try scuba before committing to a course

If you are curious about breathing underwater, ask about a supervised introductory experience. PADI describes Discover Scuba Diving as a first try in a pool or calm-water environment, with a PADI professional providing scuba gear and explaining basic skills. Treat that as a chance to find out how you feel, rather than making a particular offshore site your first goal.

For a qualification, use our learning to dive on Koh Tao guide to organise your questions before booking. Ask for the complete course schedule, teaching arrangements and what the quoted price includes. Compare the actual instruction offered instead of choosing solely on the headline price. The scuba diving guide is a useful starting point for travellers still deciding between a trial and training.

Choose a dive that fits your experience

Certified divers can put Chumphon Pinnacle on their list of sites to discuss with a dive professional. The member-contributed listing on PADI's website describes an underwater granite formation and boat entry, and lists Advanced Open Water Diver among useful training. PADI states that it cannot review all content on this platform. That is a planning clue, not an assurance that the site suits every certified diver. Explain your recent experience and ask about present conditions before committing.

Keep your booking flexible enough to accept a different site. Ask how a proposed dive fits your training and comfort, and make the decision with the professional who will lead it. This guide gives no fixed depth target or promised animal encounter.

Have a beach day without a dive booking

The Koh Tao Tourism Association lists Tanote Bay, Ao Leuk and Freedom Beach among the island's popular beaches. Pick one for an unhurried visit instead of attempting every bay in an afternoon. Decide on your return transport before settling in, and ask about current access arrangements rather than assuming every route or entrance is free.

Shark Bay (Ao Thian Ok) is another option for snorkelling: the association includes it in its snorkelling beach selection. Choose a location according to the conditions you find that day and your swimming ability. Make the outing worthwhile as a beach visit in its own right, without building it around a particular wildlife sighting.

Follow the tourism authority's advice to look without touching coral or marine life. For a group with different confidence levels, agree a meeting point on shore and let people opt out of the water without losing the whole outing.

Take a boat to Koh Nang Yuan

Koh Nang Yuan, beside Koh Tao, consists of three landmasses connected by sandbars. Combine beach time with the Koh Nang Yuan viewpoint; the tourism association describes a wooden walkway around the southern islet followed by steps through the jungle. Leave time for the climb rather than treating it as a photo stop between swims.

The association identifies longtail taxi boats from Sairee as a way to get there. Before agreeing a trip, confirm the return pickup, what the boat price covers and the current visitor arrangements. No landing fee, opening hours or crossing time is quoted here. If your group wants different activities, ask explicitly whether the boat booking allows for both the viewpoint and time on the beach.

Walk to John Suwan or Mango Viewpoint

John Suwan Viewpoint is a land-based choice on Koh Tao. The association describes the approach from the southern end of Chalok as a scramble to rocks at the top. Wear walking shoes, carry water and ask locally about the route before setting off. Choose another activity if scrambling does not suit your group.

Mango Viewpoint offers a separate walking objective from Sairee. The association's route starts in central Sairee and heads towards Mango Bay via the Hin Wong Road. Do not confuse the viewpoint with a beach booking at Mango Bay. Use the hiking guide for preparation, then confirm the route and access locally. Make either viewpoint the main outing rather than squeezing both into an already full beach day.

Paddle, then leave an evening for Sairee

Kayaking and paddleboarding provide another way to spend time on the water. The tourism association lists beachfront paddleboard hire on Koh Tao. Ask for an introduction, suitable equipment and a route recommendation based on the day's conditions. Plan a modest outing with a clear return point.

Sairee and Mae Haad are useful places to include in your planning. The association describes cafes and restaurants in Sairee and a beachside walking street towards Mae Haad. Leave an evening unbooked for a walk and dinner, especially if your days have been arranged around dive sessions. Non-divers can also consider yoga, which the national tourism authority includes among Koh Tao's activities.

Put the activities into a stay

For a suggested three-day visit, choose a beach on arrival day, reserve the next day for diving or snorkelling, and give the final day to a viewpoint or Koh Nang Yuan. This is an editorial outline, not a course timetable. Training may require a different arrangement, so settle that schedule before adding excursions. Our Koh Tao three-day itinerary provides a framework to adapt.

Koh Tao has no airport. Read the Samui, Phangan and Tao ferry guide before fixing activities around arrival and departure. Check weather information before water outings and keep an alternative day free where possible. If you are still choosing a base, use the three-island comparison.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Koh Tao worth visiting if you do not dive?

Yes. Build your visit around beaches, snorkelling, Koh Nang Yuan and a viewpoint walk. You can share the island with diving friends without sharing their course schedule.

Should a beginner book Chumphon Pinnacle?

Start by discussing an introductory experience or training with an instructor. The member-contributed listing on PADI lists advanced training as useful for Chumphon Pinnacle; do not choose an offshore site before discussing your experience and the conditions.

Which viewpoint should I choose?

Consider John Suwan if a scramble appeals, or investigate the Mango Viewpoint route from Sairee. Check access locally and choose according to your group's mobility and energy.

How many days should I allow?

Our suggested starting point is three days for a beach, a water outing and a viewpoint or Koh Nang Yuan trip. Ask for a training schedule before deciding how many nights to book for a dive course.

Can you fly directly to Koh Tao?

No. Koh Tao has no airport, so plan the onward boat connection before arranging activities on your arrival day.
guides.bestTime: Choose water outings and walks according to local conditions
guides.duration: 3 days suggested; allow additional time for dive training
guides.budget: Plan for dive instruction or boat outings, equipment hire, local transport and any access charges

guides.title: Where to Stay in Koh Phangan: Areas Compared
guides.summary: Compare eight Koh Phangan areas for families, couples, backpackers and yoga stays, with practical advice on Full Moon Party access and choosing your exact base.
guides.html:
Where to stay on Koh Phangan starts with one decision: how much of your trip revolves around the Full Moon Party? Its beach is Haad Rin Nok, also called Sunrise Beach. A room in Haad Rin and a room on the west coast solve different problems. Choose the first for proximity to the event, the second if your days centre on a different beach or yoga.

The traveller matches below are our editorial recommendations. Party proximity is qualitative, not a kilometre ranking or a promise about late-night journey times. Check the route from the exact property, including the return, before paying.

The areas side by side

AreaSuggested travellerRelationship to the Full Moon PartyBooking trade-off
Haad RinParty-focused backpackers and friendsThe event is here; check the walking route to Sunrise BeachAsk about room position and party-night noise
Baan TaiMixed groups wanting a south-coast baseBetween Thong Sala and Haad Rin; arrange a road transferCompare the exact pickup point, not just the area name
Thong SalaShort stays and travellers prioritising ferry connectionsRoad transfer to Haad RinChoose convenience at the port over a beach-led stay
SrithanuYoga travellers and longer staysWest-coast base away from the party beachArrange a return if attending the event
Haad YaoCouples and families planning beach daysWest-coast beach stay, requiring transport to Haad RinCheck the walk between the room and the sand
Haad SaladCouples and families wanting to base days around one beachWest-coast alternative to staying in the event areaChoose it for the beach, then price any party outing separately
Thong Nai PanCouples and families prioritising time at their bayNortheastern base; make a separate transfer planSpecify the exact bay and property when booking
East-coast baysIndependent travellers content to stay putHaad Tien is a boat-access example; confirm your own bay separatelyConfirm access for your particular bay and arrival time

Haad Rin: put the party within reach

Haad Rin is on Koh Phangan's southern tip. Start here if the event is the reason for coming. The useful distinction is between being in Haad Rin and being beside Sunrise Beach: ask for the actual route from your room to the entrance, rather than assuming every address gives the same walk.

For light sleepers, ask about sound from the beach and the room's position before reserving. The Full Moon Haad Rin website recommends booking early for the party. Check cancellation conditions and any minimum stay with the property itself. Read the Full Moon Party guide before choosing travel dates.

Baan Tai: a compromise for mixed groups

Baan Tai lies along the south coast between Thong Sala and Haad Rin. We suggest it when some of your group want the party and others would rather keep a separate base. Treat it as a road-transfer choice, not an extension of the party beach that you can automatically walk from.

Request a quote using the property's map pin and agree the return pickup before going out. Compare that combined room-and-transport cost with staying in Haad Rin. The Thong Sala and Baan Tai destination page covers both areas, but they are separate choices in this comparison.

Thong Sala: put the arrival and departure first

Thong Sala is Koh Phangan's main port and entry hub. Seatran Discovery lists shared taxis, called songthaews, and private transfers onward to Haad Rin, Baan Tai and Thong Nai Pan. This makes Thong Sala our practical starting point for a brief stay built around ferry connections.

Check the arrival pier on your actual ticket before choosing a room for its port location. Staying here still means a road journey to the Full Moon Party. Use the Samui, Phangan and Tao ferry guide to plan the island connection, then arrange the local leg separately.

Srithanu: choose the yoga routine first

Srithanu is a west-coast choice with a yoga community. We recommend it for travellers whose main plans involve yoga and wellness, rather than repeated trips to Haad Rin. Choose your class location first, then check how you would reach it from the room.

For a longer stay, ask about the practical details you will use every day, including a place to work if needed. Do not assume that a quiet-looking room includes reliable internet or a walkable route to classes. If the party is one optional night, settle its return transport before committing to this base.

Haad Yao: beach days on the west coast

Haad Yao is one of the west-coast beaches the Tourism Authority of Thailand recommends for sunsets. Put it on the shortlist for a couple's trip or a family holiday where the beach is the daily focus.

Compare the exact room-to-beach route, shade at the property and sleeping arrangements for children. Choosing this coast means arranging transport to the party rather than staying beside it.

Haad Salad: another west-coast beach base

Haad Salad is also on the west coast and appears in the tourism authority's sunset recommendations. We would compare it directly with Haad Yao for a stay centred on one beach. Let the property location and your preferred daily routine decide between them.

Neither beach name guarantees quiet in a particular room. Ask about nearby events for your dates and price any Haad Rin outing before booking. For families, prioritise easy access from the room over a distant view.

Thong Nai Pan: choose your bay deliberately

Thong Nai Pan is a twin-bay area in northeastern Koh Phangan. Check whether an address is at Thong Nai Pan Noi before arranging a transfer. We suggest this area for couples and families happy to make their chosen bay the centre of the holiday.

For a party-focused trip, start by checking the return journey to the exact bay. For a beach-focused trip, ask how much you can comfortably do from the property without an extra transfer. This is a choice about how you want to spend the stay, not a guarantee of silence or swimming conditions.

The east coast: access matters more than map distance

Here, east coast means the smaller bays beyond the main bases, with Haad Tien as the access example, rather than Thong Nai Pan again. A local accommodation operator describes reaching Haad Tien by taxi boat from Haad Rin, with a rough jungle-track vehicle alternative when waves prevent the boat journey. Its advice is to make the first arrival in daylight.

We recommend this type of base for independent travellers who are content to spend time in their chosen bay. Ask the property how arrivals work with luggage, what happens if the boat cannot run and how departure connects with your ferry. Do not infer an easy party-night return from a short-looking coastal gap. Confirm each bay separately.

Choose by traveller type

  • Backpackers coming for the party: start with Haad Rin, then compare Baan Tai including return transport.
  • Families: shortlist Haad Yao, Haad Salad and Thong Nai Pan, then assess the actual room and access.
  • Couples: compare the west-coast sunset beaches with a stay centred on a Thong Nai Pan bay.
  • Yoga travellers: start with Srithanu and choose around the class location.
  • Short visits: consider Thong Sala if the ferry connection is your main constraint.
  • No scooter: choose a room with the everyday places you need within a walk you have checked, and budget for arranged transfers.
  • Time away from frequent travel: consider an east-coast bay only after confirming its access arrangements.

For activities from your base, see things to do in Koh Phangan and the four-day Koh Phangan itinerary. Koh Phangan has no airport, so include the island crossing when planning the start and end of your stay.

Frequently Asked Questions

Where should I stay for the Full Moon Party?

Start with Haad Rin, where the event takes place at Sunrise Beach. Check the walking route from your room. Baan Tai and Thong Sala are alternatives if you arrange transport both ways.

Which area should families compare first?

Our shortlist is Haad Yao, Haad Salad and Thong Nai Pan. Compare room layout, beach access and the transfers your family would actually need.

Is Srithanu a party base?

We recommend it primarily for yoga stays. If attending the Full Moon Party from Srithanu, arrange your journey to Haad Rin and the return before the evening.

Does staying on the east coast mean being close to the party?

Not necessarily in practical travel terms. Haad Tien illustrates why coastal proximity and easy access are different questions. Ask about the exact bay, sea conditions and return arrangements.
guides.bestTime: Choose dates around your plans; check the party schedule and local forecast before booking
guides.duration: Allow time to enjoy your chosen base; use the four-day itinerary as a planning suggestion
guides.budget: Compare room quotes for your dates and include return transfers in the total

guides.title: Where to Stay in Koh Samui: Areas by Traveller Type
guides.summary: Choose where to stay on Koh Samui by comparing Chaweng, Lamai, Bophut, Maenam and Choeng Mon, with practical questions about beach access, meals and transport.
guides.html:
Choosing where to stay on Koh Samui starts with a simple question: what do you want to do after leaving your room? Chaweng offers nightlife, Bophut puts seaside dining in focus, and Maenam invites a quieter stay. This guide compares areas rather than individual properties. The traveller matches below are our editorial recommendations, based on the coastal character described by the Tourism Authority of Thailand and the Tourism Association of Koh Samui.

Choose the evening first

Imagine an ordinary night of your trip. If you want dancing, start with Chaweng. If dinner by the sea matters more, look at Bophut. For a slower beach holiday, shortlist Maenam or Choeng Mon. Consider the south and west when quiet time is the purpose of the booking, then work out transport before paying.

Do not use an area name as a substitute for checking an address. Ask for the walking route from the property entrance to the beach and somewhere you would eat. If travelling with children, a buggy or limited mobility, ask about steps and the approach to the room too.

The areas side by side

Chaweng: put nightlife on the shortlist

Chaweng is on Koh Samui's east coast. An older Tourism Authority of Thailand brochure describes varied accommodation here; the local tourism association recommends Chaweng for nightlife and social travellers. Choose it if a sociable holiday is the aim. Before booking, ask about music near the room rather than assuming a beachfront address will be quiet.

Compare the precise location with Chaweng Beach. If an address says Chaweng Noi, check that address separately: do not book on the assumption that your chosen evening destination will be an easy walk.

Lamai: a gentler compromise

Lamai lies south of Chaweng on the east coast. The local tourism association describes its pace as more relaxed, with places to eat and drink. Our recommendation is to consider it for a couple's holiday or a first visit where beach time matters more than clubbing. Relaxed does not mean silent, so ask about neighbouring entertainment.

Check Lamai Beach when comparing addresses. Build an outing around the Hin Ta and Hin Yai rocks at the beach's southern end, rather than choosing accommodation solely to be beside a sight.

Bophut: make dinner part of the holiday

Bophut suits a trip organised around meals and evening browsing. The tourism authority describes its beachfront road as lined with restaurants, pubs and bars, and identifies converted Chinese shophouses as part of its character. We would shortlist it for couples and families who enjoy choosing dinner outside their accommodation.

Use Fisherman's Village as a point to locate on the map, then compare the actual route from your room. Read about Bophut Beach separately if swimming is your deciding factor. A dining recommendation alone does not establish the right beach for your family.

Maenam: choose time to slow down

Maenam is on the north coast. The local tourism association describes its quiet character; an older Tourism Authority of Thailand brochure also recommends it for getting away from it all. We would choose it for reading, beach walks and a less scheduled holiday. Compare Maenam Beach addresses with your intended outings before committing to a longer stay.

Budget travellers should compare real quotes for their dates, including transport and meals. Avoid choosing Maenam simply because an area guide calls it cheap: work out the total for the particular property you want.

Choeng Mon: focus on the bay

Choeng Mon has small bays and is recommended for families by the local tourism association. It is our shortlist choice for parents and couples who prefer a smaller beach setting. Ask which beach the accommodation accesses, how you reach it and what facilities you will actually use.

For a family booking, ask about pool supervision, room layout and meal arrangements directly. Do not treat a family-friendly area description as a guarantee about a property or swimming conditions.

The south and west: make quiet a deliberate choice

The tourism authority's brochure describes isolated beaches on Koh Samui's south and west coasts and places Taling Ngam in the southwest. We would shortlist these coasts for travellers who want time together away from an entertainment strip. Taling Ngam is one starting point; compare Lipa Noi Beach too, checking the exact address rather than treating the whole west coast as one neighbourhood.

The southern shore deserves a separate beach check. Do not assume every sea-view booking offers the swimming you want. Ask about the shoreline at the property, and arrange transport for meals and outings before committing to a secluded address.

How to choose for your trip

  • First visit: compare Chaweng for nightlife with Lamai for a slower pace.
  • Families: start with Choeng Mon for its bay setting or Bophut for eating out, then check the property details.
  • Couples: Bophut if dinner is the evening plan; Maenam or the south and west if quiet is the priority.
  • Budget travellers: compare the whole booking cost, including transfers, meals and planned outings.
  • Without driving: make your shortlist depend on verified walking routes and arranged rides. Do not assume you need to rent a scooter.

Plan outings with things to do in Koh Samui and the five-day Koh Samui itinerary. Before booking travel, use how to get to Koh Samui and transportation. Check your dates against the seasonal planning guide.

Frequently Asked Questions

Where should I stay in Koh Samui for nightlife?

Start your search in Chaweng. Ask about the room's position and nearby music before booking if sleep matters as much as going out.

Which Koh Samui area should families consider?

Our first shortlist would be Choeng Mon and Bophut. Compare the actual beach route, meal options and room layout rather than relying on an area label.

Is Lamai a good alternative to Chaweng?

Consider Lamai if you want a more relaxed pace. Compare individual addresses and evening plans before deciding between the two.

Where should I stay without hiring a vehicle?

Choose a property with verified walking access to the things you plan to use daily. Ask for transport quotes for other outings before making the booking.

Should I split my stay between different areas?

Split only if changing accommodation serves a clear purpose, such as combining sociable evenings with quiet days. Otherwise, use one base and plan outings from it.

guides.title: Which Thai Island Is Best? Compare 8 Islands in Thailand
guides.summary: Compare eight islands in Thailand by traveller type, season, access and budget. Choose between Koh Samui, Phuket and smaller islands with clear trade-offs.
guides.html:
Koh Samui, Koh Phangan and Koh Tao sit in Thailand's southern Gulf; Phuket, Koh Phi Phi, Koh Lanta and Koh Lipe are Andaman choices; Koh Chang belongs to the Eastern Gulf. Those groups should not share one weather calendar. Choose the coast for your dates before deciding which island best matches your holiday.

Our first-visit shortlist is Koh Samui for a resort holiday with an airport on the island, Phuket for beach choice and nightlife, or Koh Tao when diving is the reason for travelling. These are editorial recommendations, not a ranking of quality. The eight islands below suit different priorities, and none deserves a booking simply because its name is familiar.

Eight islands at a glance

The season column is an editorial planning shortlist, not a promise of sunshine. Southern Gulf suggestions use Ko Samui station as a regional proxy; Andaman suggestions use Phuket station, not separate island measurements. Koh Chang uses separate TAT background guidance. Budget labels describe the style of trip we would price first, not verified daily costs or a cheapest-to-dearest league table. Budget means simple accommodation and selective paid activities; mid-range means a private room and money for transfers and excursions; higher budget means prioritising resort comfort or extra transport.

IslandTraveller fitSeason to considerAccess to planBudget approachMain compromise
Koh SamuiFirst visits, families and resort-focused couplesFebruary to April; compare June to September for summer travelSamui Airport, or an onward ferry connectionMid-range to higher budget; compare the complete arrival costChoose it for convenience, not a castaway setting

Koh Samui: choose comfort and variety

On Koh Samui, beach time can sit alongside cooking classes, yoga or Muay Thai training. That variety makes it our practical family and first-visit suggestion, especially if avoiding a boat on arrival matters. Samui Airport serves the island itself. Compare your complete journey rather than assuming that a different arrival airport will save money after onward transfers.

Use where to stay on Koh Samui to choose the setting before choosing the room. Start with Bophut or Maenam as areas to investigate, then compare the exact property's beach access and surroundings. Samui is not our recommendation for someone whose main aim is to leave developed holiday infrastructure behind. For couples, comfort is a reason to choose it, not evidence that every beach will feel secluded.

Koh Phangan: decide which holiday you want

Koh Phangan, officially Ko Pha-ngan, combines the Full Moon Party at Haad Rin with mountainous terrain, waterfalls and other beach bays. Choose it for the party if that is your purpose, but do not use the event's reputation as a description of every stay. Couples can instead compare Thong Nai Pan and the west coast, using the actual accommodation location as the deciding factor.

There is no airport on Koh Phangan. Plan a boat arrival and the onward journey to your beach. Our budget-to-mid-range label is a starting brief for your accommodation search, not a claim that event nights are cheap. If you want a late arrival followed by a simple airport-to-hotel transfer, Samui deserves a look first. Use the Full Moon Party guide to recheck arrangements rather than choosing dates from a remembered calendar.

Koh Tao: put the water first

Koh Tao is our diving-led pick. PADI describes reef, pinnacle and wreck sites around the island, and lists training options for different experience levels. Read learning to dive on Koh Tao before allocating your days. A cheaper room does not make a diving trip cheap if the course or guided dives have been left out of the budget.

There is no airport on Koh Tao. Lomprayah lists a Chumphon connection as well as the Samui and Phangan circuit. Start your accommodation comparison around Sairee and Mae Haad, then decide how much exploring you want beyond your base. Non-divers can consider snorkelling and beach time, but if water activities do not interest you, Samui or Phuket may be a better use of your holiday. No month in this guide guarantees underwater visibility or wildlife sightings.

Phuket: beach choice with an airport

Phuket is an Andaman island with its own airport, a choice of beaches and an established nightlife scene. Patong, Karon, Kamala and Mai Khao are different areas to compare, not interchangeable hotel addresses. TAT describes the southern beaches as generally busier than the north. For a family or couple, investigate the immediate setting before deciding that Phuket as a whole is too lively or too quiet.

Our recommendation is Phuket when access and holiday variety matter more than a small-island feel. It is not a substitute for Koh Tao if your main goal is a dive-focused island stay, and it is not a promise that every beach suits swimming on every day. Compare Koh Samui versus Phuket using your travel month and actual flight options. Price accommodation by area and include the airport transfer.

Koh Phi Phi: scenery and social evenings

Koh Phi Phi is an island group in the Andaman Sea. Its limestone scenery is a reason to put it on the shortlist. TAT describes nightlife around Tonsai and quieter alternatives at smaller beaches. For social travellers that can be the attraction; for light sleepers it is a reason to inspect the room's location carefully.

Bundhaya Speed Boat lists connections from Phuket and the Krabi area. A boat-dependent arrival makes Phi Phi a less straightforward choice than an island with an airport when you have little spare time. Do not equate a photograph of an empty bay with the experience outside your hotel. Our suggestion is to compare it with Lanta if quiet evenings matter more than nightlife. See the Koh Phi Phi overview for orientation.

Koh Lanta: a beach base for slower days

Koh Lanta's main holiday island, Koh Lanta Yai, has beaches along an island crossed by a north-to-south road. TAT identifies it as a destination for families, couples and backpackers, alongside divers. We would shortlist it for a beach-led holiday where evenings can be secondary to the place you stay.

The compromise is the geography: a road linking beach areas does not make the whole island a walkable village. Budget for local transport when comparing rooms. Access includes a car-ferry approach and Bundhaya Speed Boat connections, including from Phuket and Phi Phi. Lanta is not our first suggestion for travellers choosing primarily for nightlife. Read the Koh Lanta overview rather than assuming it has the same atmosphere as nearby Phi Phi.

Koh Lipe: choose the beach, accept the approach

Koh Lipe is an Andaman choice in Satun, with sandy bays and coral around the island. The government visitor page describes facilities and boat transfer points at Pattaya Beach. Choose it because beach time and snorkelling are central to your plans, not because a small island must be empty or undeveloped.

Bundhaya Speed Boat lists Pak Bara to Koh Lipe and land transfers from Hat Yai Airport to Pak Bara. It also lists seasonal Andaman island connections. Check the operator for your dates instead of assuming every route runs throughout the year. Our recommendation is to give Lipe a deliberate stay rather than squeeze it between fixed flights. It is not our first choice for someone who wants airport convenience. The Koh Lipe overview covers the island at launch.

Koh Chang: the Eastern Gulf alternative

Koh Chang is in Trat in the Eastern Gulf, with beaches, forest and waterfalls. It is worth comparing if your ideal week includes time inland as well as by the sea. Approach it as a separate regional choice, not an extra stop on the Samui, Phangan and Tao circuit.

Trat Airport is a mainland gateway, so allow for onward travel and the ferry. Suvarnabhumi Burapha also lists a Bangkok airport to Koh Chang coach service and hotel shuttles from the island's pier. We suggest comparing November to April first, within the broader November-to-May travel window in TAT's older Trat brochure. That brochure is background seasonal guidance, not evidence of today's ferry services. Recheck a local forecast. Koh Chang does not inherit Samui's summer recommendation merely because both are in the Gulf. Use the Koh Chang overview for the Eastern Gulf introduction.

Choose the season before the room

The climate reference is the Thai Meteorological Department's 1991 to 2020 normals: Ko Samui station 48550 and Phuket station 48564, not Phuket Airport. Ko Samui's wettest block is October to December; Phuket's wetter block runs from May to October. These stations provide regional context, not separate measurements for every island or beach.

  • February to April: our starting shortlist includes both the southern Gulf and Andaman islands.
  • June to September: compare Samui, Phangan and Tao first for a weather-led trip, without expecting rain-free days.
  • December and January: our weather-led preference is the Andaman coast over the Samui archipelago.
  • October: allow flexibility on either coast rather than treating it as a dependable crossover month.
  • Koh Chang: make a separate Eastern Gulf decision using local conditions.

These are editorial choices from the station pattern, not weather guarantees. Read the month-by-month season guide and check the weather page before booking boat-dependent plans.

Budget: compare the whole holiday

There is no verified daily-price ranking behind this comparison. A budget brief should cover the room, arrival transport, getting around, food and the activities you actually want. A mid-range or higher-budget brief should still include transfers and a buffer before important onward travel. Do not compare an island's cheapest room with another island's beachfront resort and call the difference a destination price.

  • Backpackers: begin with Phangan, Tao, Lanta or Chang, then compare the complete journey for your dates. Treat this as a shortlist to price, not a claim that they are always cheaper.
  • Families: price Samui and Phuket alongside Lanta. Compare the benefit of an on-island airport with the specific Lanta stay you want.
  • Couples: price resort comfort on Samui against a chosen bay on Phangan, beach time on Lanta or Lipe, and the exact beach area on Phuket.
  • Divers: keep training and guided dives separate from the accommodation budget on Tao.
  • Phi Phi and Lipe: include every boat and land-transfer leg before deciding whether a room fits the budget.

Combine neighbours, or stay longer in one place

For the southern Gulf, Lomprayah lists Samui to Phangan, Phangan to Tao and Chumphon to Tao. Our suggestion is to choose two islands for a week rather than spend the holiday checking in and out. Use the Gulf ferry guide or the ten-day archipelago itinerary to build a route.

For the Andaman coast, Bundhaya Speed Boat lists Phuket, Phi Phi and Lanta links, with seasonal routes continuing towards Lipe. Confirm the operating route for the actual date. Koh Chang belongs in a separate plan. For a two-week trip combining coasts, count transfer days before adding another island. Our advice is to spend the night near your departure airport before an important flight when the preceding journey depends on a boat.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which Thai island is best for a first visit?

Our starting choices are Koh Samui for resort comfort and an on-island airport, or Phuket for Andaman beaches and nightlife. Decide by season and your actual arrival options, then choose the beach area.

Which Thai island is best for families?

Compare Samui and Phuket for airport access, and Lanta for an unhurried beach base. A suitable room location and manageable arrival plan matter more than a universal family winner.

Which island should couples choose?

Our shortlist is Samui for comfort, a carefully chosen Phangan bay for a beach stay, or Lanta and Lipe for a beach-first Andaman trip. Avoid choosing a nightlife centre if silence is the priority.

Which island is cheapest?

We have not confirmed a comparable daily-cost ranking. Price Phangan, Tao, Lanta and Chang as budget-trip candidates, then include arrival transport and activities. None is guaranteed cheapest for your dates.

Which Thai island should I visit in July or August?

Our regional weather-led starting point is the Samui archipelago: Samui, Phangan or Tao. This does not guarantee calm seas or dry weather, and it is not advice for Koh Chang.

Can I fly straight to Koh Phangan or Koh Tao?

No. Neither island has an airport. Plan a boat leg, and compare arrival through Samui with mainland gateway options using the operator's current route information.

destinations.name: Bophut and Fisherman's Village
destinations.tagline: Koh Samui waterfront shopfronts and beach days around Fisherman's Village
destinations.summary: Choose Bophut on Koh Samui for Fisherman's Village shopfronts and waterfront walks, with a beach nearby and road transfers for wider island sightseeing.
destinations.html:
Bophut and Fisherman's Village are on Koh Samui's northern coast. Fisherman's Village is the focus for a visit: old Chinese shophouses have been adapted for contemporary shops and dining, with the beach beside the waterfront area. It is a useful base to compare when evening strolls and a recognisable village centre matter as much as spending the day on the sand.

The Tourism Authority of Thailand groups Bophut among Samui's quieter beach choices compared with Chaweng and Lamai. That describes the beach setting, not guaranteed quiet outside every room. Look at the exact address and its relationship to the village before booking. Use a map pin and check the route to Fisherman's Village before choosing accommodation.

What to do

  • Explore Fisherman's Village on foot, looking at the surviving shopfronts as well as the present-day shops.
  • Spend time at Bophut Beach alongside the village visit rather than treating the area as an evening-only stop.
  • Compare the north coast with Maenam before committing to a base.
  • Arrange a separate trip to the Big Buddha temple on the north-eastern side of Koh Samui.
  • Visit Chaweng on another day if you want to compare its more active beach setting.

Arriving and moving around

For a flight arrival, use Samui Airport and arrange a taxi or transfer to your address. Airport transfer listings include Bophut. For a ferry arrival or onward island trip, check the actual pier with the operator rather than asking for a generic Bophut transfer. Check the operator's current pier information even when you have used the route before.

Choose accommodation near the village if you want to make the waterfront part of an evening walk. Use taxis or arranged transfers for wider exploration and agree the fare before departure. Confirm the return arrangements when visiting a beach or attraction away from your base. A map check of the final approach is particularly useful for travellers with a pushchair or limited mobility.

We suggest Bophut for couples who enjoy walking around a settled centre, and for families who want to compare beach time with an evening in the village. Check current walking-street arrangements locally rather than building the whole stay around an assumed market night. For the wider choice, see where to stay on Koh Samui and the island overview.

Travel notice, November 2026: Lomprayah has announced temporary schedule and pier changes from 5 November to 5 December 2026. Reconfirm the exact pier and sailing before arranging a transfer.

destinations.name: Chaweng and Chaweng Noi
destinations.tagline: Koh Samui east-coast beaches with entertainment in Chaweng and a quieter setting at Chaweng Noi
destinations.summary: Compare the beach and entertainment around Chaweng with neighbouring Chaweng Noi on Koh Samui, and plan transfers before choosing your precise location.
destinations.html:
Chaweng and Chaweng Noi are beach areas on Koh Samui's east coast. Chaweng combines sand and sea with a developed holiday centre and evening entertainment. Chaweng Noi is the neighbouring beach to consider when the main beach strip sounds too active. Treat them as different locations when comparing accommodation: a name containing Chaweng does not tell you what your walk to the beach or evening plans will involve.

This is a useful starting point for first-time visitors who want their beach holiday to include activity outside the room. Groups interested in nightlife should look carefully at central Chaweng; couples seeking a quieter routine can compare the surrounding locations with Maenam and Bophut on the north coast. If you are travelling with children, check the exact beach access and the route back after dinner before choosing either Chaweng or Chaweng Noi.

What to do

  • Make Chaweng Beach the focus of a relaxed day, with time to explore the streets behind it.
  • Compare the main beach with Chaweng Noi before deciding which setting fits your trip.
  • Plan an outing to Wat Phra Yai, keeping temple visits separate from a beach-only day.
  • Spend another afternoon around Lamai to see how Koh Samui's south-eastern coast differs.
  • Use things to do on Koh Samui to choose an inland excursion instead of trying to cross the island repeatedly.

Arriving and getting around

Samui Airport serves the island. Bangkok Airways lists taxis and airport minivan transfers for Chaweng and other beach areas. Give your driver the full address and a map pin, especially for Chaweng Noi. If you arrive by ferry, arrange the transfer from the pier named on the ticket. Do not assume that the airport and ferry arrival points have the same road journey.

For local days, choose a place close to the stretch of beach and evening streets you intend to use, then walk the routes you are comfortable with. Use a taxi or an arranged transfer for outings beyond that immediate area. Agree the fare and destination before leaving, and arrange your return if the trip ends after dark. A scooter need not be part of the plan.

Nightlife access and sleep can pull a booking in different directions. Ask about nearby evening noise, and inspect the map rather than relying on an area name. Read where to stay on Koh Samui for the island-wide comparison and the Koh Samui guide for arrival options. For swimming, follow local warnings on the day and stay out when red flags are displayed.

destinations.name: Haad Rin
destinations.tagline: Koh Phangan's Full Moon Party setting: choose your dates and exact beach location
destinations.summary: Plan Haad Rin on Koh Phangan around the Full Moon Party, checking your dates, room location and transfers before choosing a beach stay.
destinations.html:
Haad Rin is on the south-east of Koh Phangan, in the Gulf of Thailand. It is the setting for the Full Moon Party, associated with this beach area. Read about Haad Rin Nok when comparing locations. Choose Haad Rin for the dates you will actually be there, not simply for its reputation.

The TAT map labels Haad Rin Nai and Haad Rin Nok separately. Keep the full beach name when checking a map or a room location. A booking described only as being in Haad Rin does not tell you which shore it faces or how close it is to an event. If you want to attend, put the walk back to your room into the decision. If you want sleep, ask specifically about sound during your stay.

Planning around the party

During the Full Moon Party, the purpose of coming here is the beach gathering and dancing. Make that a deliberate night in your itinerary, with an agreed meeting place and a plan for getting back. Read the party guide and dates before booking travel around it, and recheck the announced edition. Do not work out the date from a moon-phase app alone.

Check what is happening during your dates before choosing a room. If you are coming for nightlife, ask about events; if you are avoiding it, ask the same question. Consider a beach afternoon and an unhurried meal without assuming that every non-party date will be quiet.

What to do

  • Read the Haad Rin Nok beach guide before choosing your location.
  • Locate your chosen beach and room on a map before booking.
  • Set aside a separate outing for Thong Sala and Baan Tai.
  • For a change of coast, compare Srithanu and the west-coast beaches rather than trying to fit every beach into one day.

Our recommendation is to book Haad Rin when the party itself, or this particular beach setting, is the reason for the trip. For a holiday centred on beach days away from the event setting, also consider Thong Nai Pan. If travelling with children, make the dates and the room's immediate surroundings part of your checks rather than relying on an island-wide label.

For arrival, check the pier printed on your boat ticket and arrange the transfer from that pier. Use the ferry guide alongside where to stay in Koh Phangan. Keep the morning after the party flexible instead of committing to an ambitious island excursion.

destinations.name: Koh Chang
destinations.tagline: An eastern Gulf island off Trat, with separate onward planning for Koh Mak and Koh Kood
destinations.summary: Choose Koh Chang in Thailand for beaches and greenery, with a Trat airport and ferry approach and a weather pattern distinct from Samui.
destinations.html:
Koh Chang lies off Trat in Thailand's eastern Gulf. Its beaches and greenery are a reason to stay here rather than treating it only as a stepping stone to Koh Mak or Koh Kood. Those nearby islands are alternatives to compare, with their own arrival arrangements; this site does not yet offer separate destination pages for them.

Getting to Koh Chang

Trat Airport is on the mainland in Khao Saming, so an airport arrival still needs an onward transfer and sea crossing. TAT identifies Ao Thammachat as a mainland ferry pier for Koh Chang. Check the current operator's departure and vehicle arrangements before travelling, particularly if your flight lands late. Do not use an old tourism-brochure timetable as proof of today's last boat. For an onward trip to Koh Mak or Koh Kood, confirm the actual operator, departure pier and travel-date availability rather than assuming every island is joined by a year-round ferry.

Eastern Gulf season and park sites

Koh Chang is in the Gulf, but it does not follow Samui's rainfall calendar. TMD's mainland Trad station normals for 1991 to 2020 show a strongly wet May to October and much drier November to February. The Ko Samui station instead records its heaviest monthly rainfall in October to December. TAT's Trat brochure recommends the November to April period for calmer conditions around Koh Chang. Treat that as seasonal guidance, not a guarantee about the sea on your crossing day. Compare dates in the Thai island season guide.

Confirm the current Mu Ko Chang National Park admission charge directly with DNP. The National Park Office lists the Historical Royal Journey to Ko Chang hiking trail closed annually from 1 June to 31 October. Its current list also records a temporary scuba closure in the Koh Yak Yai coral-restoration area from 11 November, with no end date stated. These are site restrictions, not a closure of every Koh Chang beach or hotel.

Who should choose Koh Chang?

We recommend Koh Chang for travellers who want beaches and forest in an eastern Gulf itinerary and accept the mainland transfer plus ferry. Compare Koh Samui if an island airport matters, Koh Phangan if your trip is already centred on the Samui archipelago, and Koh Tao for a dive-learning plan. Read which Thai island is best and Samui versus Phangan versus Tao before choosing.

destinations.name: Koh Lanta
destinations.tagline: An Andaman base with beaches, an east-coast old town and seasonal offshore trips
destinations.summary: Choose Koh Lanta in Thailand for a beach-and-old-town stay, then plan offshore park trips separately around their access dates and your boat connections.
destinations.html:
Koh Lanta is on Thailand's Andaman side in Krabi province. For this overview, the holiday base is Koh Lanta Yai: beaches and the east-coast old town give you different ways to spend a day. The national park and offshore islands need their own planning, rather than being treated as an automatic part of every beach stay.

Getting to Koh Lanta

Krabi Airport is an arrival option, with onward road transfers to Lanta described by Satun Pakbara Speed Boat Club. The same operator lists boats between Lanta, Phuket and Koh Phi Phi. Its published Lanta check-in is at Saladan pier on Koh Lanta Yai. Confirm the complete transfer, including any ferry leg, for your date. If you intend to continue to Koh Lipe, verify that particular connection rather than assuming a displayed route is a year-round service.

Weather and offshore closures

TMD's Ko Lanta station normals for 1991 to 2020 show a wetter May to October and a drier December to March. That is an Andaman pattern, different from the October to December rainfall peak at the Ko Samui station. Choose dates with the Thai island season guide, then check the sea forecast nearer departure.

As of November 2026, the National Park Office lists Ko Rok and its accommodation and campsite closed from 1 June to 30 September annually. Ko Ha and the Hin Daeng-Hin Muang sites are listed closed from 1 August to 30 September. These are named offshore sites, not a blanket closure of Koh Lanta Yai. Ask DNP to confirm the current special-area charge for Ko Rok, Ko Ngai, Ko Ha and Hin Daeng-Hin Muang. Confirm each entrance separately, including any offshore charge.

Who should choose Koh Lanta?

We recommend Lanta for travellers who want to divide a stay between beach time and an old-town visit, with offshore days as optional extras. Compare the transfer with Koh Samui's airport option, consider Koh Phangan if you want to stay within a Gulf itinerary, and compare Koh Tao if diving lessons are central. Read which Thai island is best and the Samui, Phangan and Tao comparison.

destinations.name: Koh Lipe
destinations.tagline: A southern Andaman island reached by boat, with Tarutao park trips to plan separately
destinations.summary: Plan Koh Lipe in Thailand around a mainland-to-island transfer, a beach base and the specific Tarutao park sites open during your visit.
destinations.html:
Koh Lipe is in Satun province on Thailand's southern Andaman side, close to Malaysia. Its main beach areas include Pattaya, Sunrise and Sunset. Use this overview to decide whether you want to make the boat journey and stay here, rather than adding Lipe as an unplanned stop at the end of a Gulf itinerary.

Airport, pier and ferry season

Hat Yai Airport is a mainland arrival option, followed by a road transfer to Pak Bara pier and a boat to Koh Lipe. Satun Pakbara Speed Boat Club lists Pak Bara-Lipe services and combined Hat Yai airport connections. Bundhaya Speed Boat also lists Pak Bara-Lipe and advertises high-season booking. Pattaya Beach is a published passenger-boat arrival area; confirm the exact check-in and landing instructions with your operator.

Plan cross-island connections during the Andaman travel season, but verify the actual operating dates. Satun Pakbara lists connections with Koh Lanta, Koh Phi Phi and Phuket; its seasonal notes still include old dates, so they do not establish a 2026 to 2027 calendar. Do not assume those longer routes run in the rainy season, or that a park closure automatically stops every Pak Bara boat. Obtain confirmation before arranging flights around a sailing.

Weather and Tarutao park access

Use TMD's mainland Satun station normals for 1991 to 2020 as a regional guide, not a forecast for Koh Lipe. They show a wetter May to October, particularly September and October, and a drier January and February. This is the Andaman side, unlike the October to December rainfall peak at TMD's Ko Samui station. See the island season guide.

Confirm the current Tarutao National Park admission charge directly with DNP. Check how the park charge is handled for your itinerary. The National Park Office's current annual list closes named Adang-Rawi-area sites, including Jabang and Rawi's white-sand beach, from 1 June to 30 September. A separate group, including north and east Adang and specified Talang and Hin Ru sites, closes from 1 October to 31 December. Ask which sites an excursion will visit; neither entry in the list says that all of Koh Lipe closes.

Who should choose Koh Lipe?

Our recommendation is Lipe for travellers willing to build their holiday around the boat transfer and beach time. Compare the journey with Koh Samui, consider Koh Phangan for a Gulf-based stay, and compare Koh Tao if learning to dive is your main aim. Start with which Thai island is best and the Gulf island comparison.

destinations.name: Koh Phangan
destinations.tagline: Choose your coast: Haad Rin's party, west-coast beaches or Thong Nai Pan's bays
destinations.summary: Choose a base on Koh Phangan that fits your trip, from Haad Rin's Full Moon Party to west-coast beach days and the separate bays of Thong Nai Pan.
destinations.html:
Koh Phangan, officially Ko Pha-ngan, is an island in the Gulf of Thailand in Surat Thani province, north of Koh Samui. Its reputation starts with the Full Moon Party, but that is a poor guide to choosing every stay here. There are mountains through the interior, beaches around the coast and a working arrival town at Thong Sala. Decide what you want outside your door before choosing a room.

The first distinction is between Haad Rin and the rest of your island plans. Read about Haad Rin Nok when comparing beach locations. Check the dates of your actual stay rather than treating a party photograph as a year-round description. For a beach-led alternative, compare Srithanu, Haad Yao and Haad Salad on the west coast with Thong Nai Pan in the north-east.

What to do

  • Start by comparing Haad Yao and Haad Salad, then leave time for the west-coast sunset.
  • Give Thong Nai Pan Noi and neighbouring Thong Nai Pan Yai a beach day of their own.
  • Read the access information for Bottle Beach before making it the day's destination.
  • Consider a walk at Phaeng Waterfall or Khao Ra, checking conditions and access before setting out.
  • Build a slower day around yoga and meditation rather than another transfer.

For a first visit, our suggestion is to choose one base and explore selectively. Couples and families can compare the west coast with Thong Nai Pan; travellers coming specifically for the party should start with Haad Rin. If the ferry connection is your priority, weigh Thong Sala against a beach base. These are planning choices, not promises that any neighbourhood will be silent. Ask about nearby events for your dates before booking.

Koh Phangan has no airport. Plan a boat arrival, and compare the onward journey from Samui Airport with a mainland connection. Use the Gulf islands ferry guide to check the current operator, arrival pier and onward transfer. Leave breathing room between a flight and a boat rather than making the whole trip depend on a tight connection.

The where to stay guide helps narrow down the coast. Then use things to do in Koh Phangan and the four-day itinerary to build a trip around it. For a longer island hop, compare Koh Tao and Koh Samui before adding another ferry day.

Access check, 16 November 2026: DNP lists all Than Sadet-Ko Pha-ngan National Park tourist sites and accommodation temporarily closed from 12 November onwards due to heavy rain, with no reopening date. Confirm a reopening notice with the park before planning a waterfall visit or entering a park trail.

destinations.name: Koh Phi Phi
destinations.tagline: An Andaman island stay with separate planning for Maya Bay on Phi Phi Le
destinations.summary: Plan Koh Phi Phi in Thailand around your boat arrival and the distinction between Phi Phi Don and a protected-area excursion to Maya Bay on Phi Phi Le.
destinations.html:
Koh Phi Phi is an island group off Krabi on Thailand's Andaman side. Separate a stay on Phi Phi Don from a boat visit to Phi Phi Le, where Maya Bay is located. Booking a room on Phi Phi Don does not itself secure a Maya Bay visit, and a bay closure does not mean that every Phi Phi stay is cancelled.

Getting to Koh Phi Phi

Plan an airport arrival at Phuket Airport or Krabi Airport, followed by a separate land and sea transfer. Satun Pakbara Speed Boat Club lists a Phuket to Phi Phi service and onward connections with Koh Lanta. Its published check-in points are Rassada pier on Phuket and Ao Tonsai on Phi Phi. Confirm the arrival point against your accommodation and check the sailing for your travel date. Do not assume an onward island connection runs throughout the monsoon.

Season, Maya Bay and park fees

For a regional climate reference, use TMD's Krabi station normals for 1994 to 2020, not an invented Phi Phi weather station. They show the wetter May to October pattern of the Andaman coast, with a drier December to March. This differs from the October to December rainfall peak at TMD's Ko Samui station. Island sea conditions still need a current forecast.

As of November 2026, the National Park Office's annual closure list gives 1 August to 30 September for Maya Bay, Loh Samah and Lo Ko. TAT reported Maya Bay reopening on 1 October 2026. Check the next applicable notice before booking around a particular bay. Visits fall within Hat Noppharat Thara-Mu Ko Phi Phi National Park. Confirm the current special-area charge for Phi Phi Don, Phi Phi Le and Bamboo Island directly with DNP. Ask whether the boat ticket includes the park charge.

Who should choose Koh Phi Phi?

Our recommendation is Phi Phi for a trip built around an island stay and a carefully checked boat excursion. Compare it with Koh Samui if you would prefer an airport-based holiday, Koh Phangan for another island option, and Koh Tao if dive training is the reason for travelling. Read which Thai island is best, the three Gulf islands compared and the season guide before combining coasts.

destinations.name: Koh Samui
destinations.tagline: Choose between an active east coast, north-coast villages and inland excursions
destinations.summary: Choose a base on Koh Samui by comparing Chaweng, Lamai, Bophut and Maenam, then plan airport transfers, temple visits and ferries to the neighbouring islands.
destinations.html:
Koh Samui (Ko Samui) is a Gulf of Thailand island in Surat Thani province. It suits a first island holiday when you want beaches alongside places to explore on land. The key decision is your base: Chaweng and Chaweng Noi, Lamai, Bophut and Maenam offer different balances of activity and quiet. Start with what you want within walking distance each evening, then budget separately for excursions.

Chaweng, on the east coast, is the choice for beach days with entertainment close by. Consider neighbouring Chaweng Noi for a quieter beach setting, checking the actual route to central Chaweng before booking. Lamai, further south, combines a beach base with outings to the south-eastern coast. Bophut centres on Fisherman's Village, with converted Chinese shophouses and an evening stroll around the waterfront. Maenam on the north coast is worth comparing if your priority is a quieter beach setting. Families and couples can use any of these bases; choose the surroundings that fit your daily routine rather than a label alone.

What to do

  • Compare Chaweng Beach with Lamai Beach before choosing your base.
  • Visit Wat Phra Yai, the Big Buddha temple, on an outing away from the beach.
  • Explore Fisherman's Village and its shopfronts in Bophut.
  • Plan a separate outing to Na Muang Waterfalls, checking conditions before setting off.
  • Consider an Ang Thong day trip after checking current park access and sailing conditions.

Getting here and around

Samui Airport (USM) is on the island. Bangkok Airways operates direct flights from Bangkok Suvarnabhumi. Airport taxis and minivan transfers provide onward travel to the beach areas. For an overland approach, compare Lomprayah's mainland connections with its inter-island services to Koh Phangan and Koh Tao. Confirm the pier on your particular ticket before arranging a road transfer. Check the operator's latest travel information before departure.

Choose taxis or arranged transfers for outings between areas and agree the fare before departure. February to April is our suggested planning window, not a weather guarantee. The Thai Meteorological Department's Ko Samui station, 1991 to 2020, records its wettest months in October to December. Use the weather guide and where to stay on Koh Samui to narrow the choice, then build a trip with the five-day itinerary.
