Access check, November 2026: DNP lists all Ang Thong tourist sites and accommodation closed annually from 1 November to 15 December. Choose another outing during that period and confirm reopening before booking.

destinations.name: Koh Tao and Koh Nang Yuan
destinations.tagline: A Gulf island for diving and bay visits, with Sairee, Mae Haad and offshore Koh Nang Yuan
destinations.summary: Choose a Koh Tao base around Sairee or Mae Haad, plan diving and beach outings, and understand the ferry arrival before adding a visit to Koh Nang Yuan.
destinations.html:
Koh Tao (Ko Tao) is a Gulf of Thailand island in Surat Thani province, north of Koh Phangan. Diving is a central reason to come, but you can also build a stay around beaches, walking and boat outings. Sairee and Mae Haad are the west-coast areas to compare first. Offshore, Koh Nang Yuan is a separate visit, with three islets joined by a sandbar and a viewpoint above them.

Choose Sairee if the beach and a social holiday atmosphere are priorities. Mae Haad is the ferry arrival area and is worth comparing when keeping arrival and departure simple matters most. For a trip centred on quieter bays, investigate the exact location and transfer arrangements before booking elsewhere on the island. Do not judge convenience by straight-line distance alone. We suggest the Sairee and Mae Haad area for first-time visitors who would like to organise their stay without relying on a scooter.

What to do

  • Use learning to dive on Koh Tao to plan questions for an instructor before choosing a course.
  • Combine Sairee Beach with time to explore the neighbouring arrival area of Mae Haad.
  • Consider a weather-dependent boat outing to Koh Nang Yuan and its viewpoint, checking access arrangements before setting off.
  • Plan snorkelling with local advice on conditions, keeping clear of coral and marine life.
  • Set aside time for a walk or a beach day if you would prefer a break from water activities.

How to get here

Koh Tao has no airport, and neither does Koh Phangan. For Koh Tao, compare a flight to Samui Airport followed by a ferry with a mainland connection via Chumphon Airport. Lomprayah lists services linking Koh Tao with Koh Samui, Koh Phangan and Chumphon. Its Koh Tao office and pier are in Mae Haad. Check which road transfer is included in a combined ticket and allow room for a changed sailing before an onward flight.

Check Lomprayah's current pier information and sailing schedules before departure. There is no fixed timetable or fare here: verify your travel date with the operator. On the island, plan local walks around your chosen base and arrange transfers for outings that do not suit walking.

The Tourism Authority of Thailand recommends February to April for Koh Tao. Treat those months as a planning starting point, not a promise about visibility or boat conditions. Divers should choose activities with an instructor's assessment, and non-divers can plan land and beach days with the Koh Tao three-day itinerary. For a longer trip, compare Samui, Phangan and Tao before deciding how to divide your time.

Travel notice, November 2026: Lomprayah has announced temporary schedule and pier changes from 5 November to 5 December 2026. Reconfirm the exact pier and sailing before arranging a transfer.

destinations.name: Krabi, Ao Nang and Railay
destinations.tagline: A mainland Andaman gateway, with Ao Nang boat departures and Railay's limestone coast
destinations.summary: Use Krabi in Thailand as a mainland base for Ao Nang, Railay and onward island travel, with an airport arrival and a choice between road and boat transfers.
destinations.html:
Krabi is on mainland Thailand's Andaman coast, not an island. This overview covers Krabi, the beach base of Ao Nang and the Railay area. Ao Nang is a launching point for boats to nearby islands and the beaches of the Phra Nang peninsula. Railay's limestone cliffs give a different focus from a holiday centred on the beaches of Koh Samui.

Airport, coast and island boats

Start with Krabi Airport (KBV), then arrange your onward transfer to the actual place you are staying. A booking for Krabi town is not a booking for Railay. Tiger Line lists Krabi airport transfers, Ao Nammao pier and Railay's east-side floating pier; check which meeting point and boat leg your ticket includes. Bundhaya Speed Boat also lists an Ao Nang to Koh Lanta route. Recheck departures by date, especially when building a longer island-hopping journey.

Andaman season and park visits

Use the Andaman calendar here. TMD's Krabi station normals for 1994 to 2020 show wetter conditions from May to October and a drier December to March. The Ko Samui station's rainfall instead peaks in October to December. That distinction matters more than simply asking whether southern Thailand is in season. Read the island season comparison and keep boat days flexible.

For trips into Hat Noppharat Thara-Mu Ko Phi Phi National Park, check which protected sites the itinerary includes. Confirm the current special-area charge for Phi Phi Don, Phi Phi Le and Bamboo Island directly with DNP. This is a park fee, not the fare for every boat from Ao Nang. The National Park Office lists Maya Bay, Loh Samah and Lo Ko closed from 1 August to 30 September annually; that is not a closure of Krabi or every island boat.

Who should choose Krabi?

We recommend Krabi when mainland access and limestone-coast scenery matter more than staying on an island. It is worth comparing with Samui for a beach base, Koh Phangan for a separate island stay and Koh Tao if learning to dive is the priority. Use which Thai island is best and Samui versus Phangan versus Tao to decide before booking a transfer between coasts.

destinations.name: Lamai
destinations.tagline: A south-east Koh Samui beach base for coastal outings and the Hin Ta and Hin Yai rocks
destinations.summary: Base yourself in Lamai on Koh Samui for beach days and the Hin Ta and Hin Yai rocks, with road transfers for temple visits and outings elsewhere on the island.
destinations.html:
Lamai is a beach area on the south-east coast of Koh Samui. It offers a developed holiday base with a different setting from Chaweng to the north. Consider it when you want a beach-centred stay with outings along the southern part of the island. The coast around the Hin Ta and Hin Yai rocks gives a Lamai visit a focus beyond the sand itself.

Lamai is an active holiday area, so do not read a comparison with Chaweng as a promise of silence. The central beach, the streets behind it and the approaches towards the rocks make different bases. Check the specific location if evenings on foot are important. For a quieter north-coast alternative, compare Maenam; for shopfronts and waterfront strolling, consider Bophut and Fisherman's Village. Lamai is our suggestion for couples and families who want to build a trip around the south-eastern coast.

What to do

  • Leave a full morning free for Lamai Beach, choosing where to settle after checking local conditions.
  • Visit Hin Ta and Hin Yai, the Grandfather and Grandmother rocks, south of the main beach.
  • Plan a road excursion to Wat Khunaram, which houses the mummified monk.
  • Set aside a separate outing for Na Muang Waterfalls after checking weather and access.
  • Compare the wider island's beach bases using where to stay on Koh Samui.

Getting to Lamai

Arrive at Samui Airport, then continue by road. Bangkok Airways lists taxis and airport minivan transfers to Lamai. Travellers arriving by ferry should check their arrival pier before requesting a transfer, particularly when continuing from another Gulf island. Give the driver a precise address rather than only asking for Lamai: your booked location may not be beside the part of the beach you have pictured.

Walk locally when the route suits you and use taxis or arranged transfers for other areas. Agree the destination and fare before starting. For an outing that combines the rocks, a temple and an inland stop, discuss the full route and return journey in advance. There is no need to make learning to ride a scooter part of your holiday.

Keep the beach day flexible rather than promising swimming at a fixed time. Follow local warnings and avoid entering the water under a red flag. Choose land activities if conditions deteriorate. Our Koh Samui overview explains the other areas, while the five-day itinerary helps organise outings without turning every day into a transfer.

destinations.name: Maenam and the north coast
destinations.tagline: A quieter Koh Samui beach base, with north-coast outings and a ferry-pier connection
destinations.summary: Compare Maenam on Koh Samui for a quieter beach holiday, then plan road trips to Bophut and check the departure pier for ferries to Koh Phangan or Koh Tao.
destinations.html:
Maenam is a beach and village area on Koh Samui's north coast. Choose it as a starting point when you would like a quieter beach setting than Chaweng or Lamai, while keeping other parts of the island available for day trips. The view across the water towards Koh Phangan helps place the north coast within the wider Gulf island group.

Maenam and the north coast should not be treated as one compact pedestrian centre. Look at the exact location of a prospective room, its beach access and the places you expect to reach on foot. A quieter setting works best when you are happy to spend time there rather than repeatedly travelling back to another area's evening activity. Couples planning a slow beach stay and families willing to arrange occasional transfers should put Maenam on their shortlist.

What to do

  • Make Maenam Beach the focus of an unhurried day.
  • Visit Bophut and Fisherman's Village as a separate outing along the northern part of Koh Samui.
  • Plan a road trip to Wat Phra Yai if you want a cultural stop during the stay.
  • Compare Maenam with Chaweng to decide how much evening activity you want near your accommodation.
  • Use the Gulf ferry guide if this is one stop on a longer island trip.

Arrivals and ferry planning

Samui Airport is the island's flight gateway. Airport transfer listings include Maenam, so arrange the road leg to your precise address. For an arrival by sea, check the named pier first and plan from there. Walking from a pier should be a decision based on your actual address, luggage and route, not simply the fact that both places say Maenam.

Lomprayah lists its Pralan Pier in Maenam and sells connections involving Koh Phangan and Koh Tao. Check its current pier information and sailing schedules before departure. Reconfirm where your particular sailing leaves before reserving a transfer or choosing accommodation around pier access. This guide deliberately gives no fixed fare or crossing time.

Walk around the immediate beach and village where the route suits you, and use taxis or arranged transfers for outings along the coast. Agree the fare before leaving and confirm the return journey. Check current sea conditions before swimming rather than assuming a quieter beach means safer water. Read where to stay on Koh Samui for the broader comparison, or return to the island guide to plan your arrival.

destinations.name: Phuket
destinations.tagline: An Andaman base for beach holidays, old-town walks and onward island boats
destinations.summary: Choose Phuket in Thailand for an airport arrival, a choice of beach areas and an old-town break, with onward boats to Phi Phi and Koh Lanta.
destinations.html:
Phuket is an island on Thailand's Andaman coast. Choose it for a holiday that combines beaches with town time: Patong, Kata and Karon are different bases from Phuket Old Town. This is our overview of the island, so start by choosing the kind of stay you want rather than treating every beach as interchangeable.

Getting to Phuket and onward

Arrive at Phuket Airport (HKT) and continue by road to your base. Staying on Phuket does not require an island ferry. For an onward sea journey, Satun Pakbara Speed Boat Club lists boats to Koh Phi Phi and Koh Lanta, with Phuket check-in at Rassada pier. Confirm the sailing for your actual date and leave room between a flight and a boat departure. A route displayed on a schedule page is not a promise of service throughout the year.

Season and national parks

Phuket follows the Andaman weather pattern, with a wetter May to October and a drier start to the year. TMD's Phuket station normals for 1991 to 2020 show that pattern; they are climate averages, not a forecast. Do not transfer Koh Samui's season to this coast: TMD's Ko Samui station has its heaviest monthly rainfall in October to December. Compare dates in the best time to visit the Thai islands.

The Similan Islands and Surin Islands are separate offshore national parks, not Phuket beaches. As of November 2026, the National Park Office lists both closed from 16 May to 14 October each year. The same list records temporary closure of the Ao Mai Ngam campsite on Surin from 15 October to 23 November, and indefinite closures at named Similan sites including Ko Tachai. Reopening the parks does not mean every site is accessible or guarantee calm seas. For a Similan visit, TAT suggests a Khao Lak base rather than assuming every excursion starts on Phuket. Check the park's access notice and ticket requirements before paying for a trip.

Who should choose Phuket?

Our recommendation is Phuket for travellers who value arriving by air and combining beach days with an old-town visit. Compare that with a Samui-based holiday, a Koh Phangan stay or a Koh Tao diving plan before adding an extra coast. Read Koh Samui versus Phuket, the Samui, Phangan and Tao comparison and which Thai island is best.

destinations.name: Sairee and Mae Haad
destinations.tagline: Koh Tao's west-coast beach and ferry-arrival areas, planned together for a practical stay
destinations.summary: Compare Sairee Beach with the Mae Haad ferry area on Koh Tao, then plan local walks, transfers and diving days without assuming you need a scooter.
destinations.html:
Sairee and Mae Haad are neighbouring areas on the west coast of Koh Tao. Sairee is the beach-focused choice; Mae Haad is the ferry arrival area. Think about them together when planning where to stay, but check the precise address rather than assuming that a room near one is equally convenient for the other. This is the part of Koh Tao to investigate first if you want a beach base and manageable arrival arrangements.

Sairee suits travellers who want their days to revolve around the beach and the island's diving scene. Mae Haad is useful to compare if a ferry connection is the main constraint on the trip. Couples seeking quiet should ask about the immediate surroundings of any room, while backpackers planning to meet people may prefer a more social location. These are editorial suggestions about how to choose a base, not a guarantee about every street.

What to do

  • Spend a day at Sairee Beach, leaving the schedule open enough to respond to local sea conditions.
  • Explore Mae Haad around your arrival or departure, keeping the ferry check-in separate from sightseeing plans.
  • Prepare for a course with learning to dive on Koh Tao, then discuss the training plan with your instructor.
  • Consider a boat visit to Koh Nang Yuan with its connected islets and viewpoint, subject to current access and conditions.
  • Use things to do on Koh Tao to plan a non-diving day.

Arriving and getting around

Koh Tao has no airport. Arrival involves a boat crossing, with onward travel on the island from Mae Haad. Lomprayah's Koh Tao contact map identifies its Mae Haad pier. Before departure, confirm the operator's arrival point and arrange any pickup with your accommodation using that information. For the journey off Koh Tao, check the pier, check-in requirements and any transfer to an airport separately.

Walk within your chosen beach or village area when the route suits you. For luggage transfers and outings beyond it, arrange a taxi or pickup in advance rather than planning every movement around a hired scooter. Ask for a map pin and inspect the route between your room, beach and course meeting point. Staying near the places you will actually use can be more helpful than simply choosing a familiar area name.

For snorkelling, keep clear of coral and other marine life and ask locally about the day's conditions. Do not assume that an easy walk to the water makes every swimming spot appropriate. On departure days, leave space for changed sailings rather than making a tight onward flight part of the plan. The Gulf ferry guide covers the wider connection, and the Koh Tao overview helps you compare the island's different settings.

destinations.name: Srithanu and the west coast (Haad Yao, Haad Salad)
destinations.tagline: A west-coast base on Koh Phangan, linking Srithanu with Haad Yao and Haad Salad
destinations.summary: Compare Srithanu, Haad Yao and Haad Salad on Koh Phangan's west coast for beach days, sunset outings and a stay with time for yoga or meditation.
destinations.html:
Srithanu is on the west coast of Koh Phangan, in the Gulf of Thailand. This area guide pairs it with Haad Yao and Haad Salad. They are separate places, not three names for one beach. Use the guide to choose a base, then check the exact location of a room against the beach or activity you expect to use most.

The west coast is a useful starting point for a trip built around beach time and sunsets. TAT identifies Haad Yao and Haad Salad as west-coast sunset beaches. Its Surat Thani brochure describes white sand at Haad Yao and a quiet beach with an offshore reef at Haad Salad. These are reasons to compare them in person, not to schedule a race between them. Pick one for the afternoon and leave room to stay if it suits you.

Choosing where to spend your days

Start with Srithanu if you want to look into yoga or meditation alongside beach time. A yoga provider lists Srithanu as a location, but do not assume a published class programme is running. Confirm availability directly before building a stay around a session. Ask about the teaching style, level and cancellation arrangements. A place on a map is not confirmation that a particular class will run on the day you arrive.

If the beach outside the room matters more than a class programme, compare Haad Yao with Haad Salad before choosing. Avoid booking under the broad label of west coast without looking at the approach to the actual property. A room close to your preferred beach may suit you better than one that requires a transfer every time you want to go there. Our recommendation is to choose the daily routine first and treat other bays as outings.

What to do

  • Spend an afternoon at Haad Yao, leaving time to watch the evening light.
  • Compare Haad Salad on another day rather than moving between beaches all afternoon.
  • Read the Mae Haad and Koh Ma guide when planning another coastal outing.
  • Keep a morning free to try a suitable yoga or meditation session after confirming the programme.

This is our suggested area to investigate for couples and travellers who want beach days with time for a class. It can also work as a family planning option, provided the particular room, beach access and transport suit the children travelling. Do not read the word wellness as a promise of silence. Ask about nearby events and the immediate setting before committing to a longer stay.

Compare the west coast with Thong Nai Pan if you are deciding between coasts, and with Haad Rin if attending the Full Moon Party is important. For arrival, match your transfer to the pier on the ticket using the ferry guide. The where to stay guide helps turn those choices into a base for the trip.

destinations.name: Thong Nai Pan
destinations.tagline: Two north-east Koh Phangan bays, with the beach at the centre of the stay
destinations.summary: Choose between Thong Nai Pan Noi and Thong Nai Pan Yai on Koh Phangan's north-east coast, and plan a beach stay with the right bay and transfer.
destinations.html:
Thong Nai Pan is on the north-east coast of Koh Phangan, in the Gulf of Thailand. The name covers two neighbouring bays, Thong Nai Pan Noi and Thong Nai Pan Yai. Make that distinction before booking: check which bay your room is on, not just whether the address includes Thong Nai Pan. For a beach-led stay, the difference between the two locations is more useful than a general description of the island.

Our suggestion is to consider Thong Nai Pan when you want the beach to anchor the day. TAT's Surat Thani brochure describes a crescent bay backed by coconut trees and identifies the area as a family outing option. That makes it worth comparing with the west-coast beaches when choosing a base. Visit for the setting rather than expecting every beach activity or every part of the island to be on your doorstep.

Noi or Yai?

Use Thong Nai Pan Noi as the first beach page to read, then compare your options around Yai. Look at the actual room location, the route to the sand and where you expect to eat. If travelling with children, ask about steps and the approach from the room to the beach. If travelling as a couple, decide whether you prefer to spend most evenings near the room or plan regular outings elsewhere.

Do not choose a bay solely from a photograph of the water. Ask about conditions during your dates, and make each day's swimming decision at the beach. The general appeal of a bay is not a guarantee of calm water. Keep some flexibility for a day when reading, walking or taking a long lunch suits the conditions better than going into the sea.

What to do

  • Give Thong Nai Pan Noi an unhurried beach day.
  • Visit Thong Nai Pan Yai to compare the neighbouring bay before deciding how to spend the rest of the stay.
  • Look into Than Sadet Waterfall as a separate outing, checking access first.
  • Use the national park guide to check the arrangements before planning time away from the beach.

For a short trip, our recommendation is to resist adding a different coast every day. If the Full Moon Party is the main reason for coming to Koh Phangan, compare Haad Rin before booking here. If you choose Thong Nai Pan and still want to attend, arrange both legs of that outing in advance. For a stay focused on port-town convenience, compare Thong Sala and Baan Tai.

Confirm your arrival pier and ask for a transfer to the correct bay, with Noi or Yai written in the request. Check the full price and the return arrangements before accepting. Use the ferry guide for the boat connection, then adapt the Koh Phangan four-day itinerary to leave more time at the beach. A slower plan is our suggested way to make this base worthwhile.

Access check, 16 November 2026: DNP lists all Than Sadet-Ko Pha-ngan National Park tourist sites and accommodation temporarily closed from 12 November onwards due to heavy rain, with no reopening date. Confirm a reopening notice with the park before planning a waterfall visit or entering a park trail.

destinations.name: Thong Sala and Baan Tai
destinations.tagline: Koh Phangan's port town and the south-coast area towards Haad Rin
destinations.summary: Use Thong Sala and Baan Tai on Koh Phangan to plan a practical arrival, time in the port town and a south-coast base with a separate trip to Haad Rin.
destinations.html:
Thong Sala is a port and trading town on Koh Phangan, in the Gulf of Thailand. This guide also covers Baan Tai, the south-coast area towards Haad Rin. Treat them as separate locations when booking: a room described as being in the Thong Sala and Baan Tai area may serve a very different trip from one close to your arrival pier.

Thong Sala is useful when the practical parts of an island stay matter. TAT describes a trading centre with a passenger pier and banks. Our suggestion is to give the town some time on arrival rather than rushing straight through it. Settle the onward transfer, get your bearings and decide whether you want a town base or a beach base. If you only have a short stay, weigh that convenience against spending the nights on the coast you most want to explore.

Town or south-coast base?

Choose Thong Sala if being near the port town is the priority. Consider Baan Tai if you prefer to base yourself along the southern side of the island, but check the exact address rather than treating the whole area as walkable from the pier. Plot both the room and your planned outings before paying. In particular, a Baan Tai booking is not a booking on Haad Rin Nok.

The town and the beach should be separate decisions. A place that works well for shopping, meals and a ferry connection may not be the place you would choose for every afternoon on the sand. Compare a stay here with Srithanu and the west coast or Thong Nai Pan. If swimming is the main purpose of the holiday, read the relevant beach page before choosing a room from its sea-view photograph.

What to do

  • Get your bearings around Thong Sala before choosing where to eat.
  • Use the Thong Sala night market guide to plan an evening, checking the current arrangements locally.
  • Walk towards the waterfront to see the retired naval ship displayed at Thong Sala.
  • Make Haad Rin a planned outing, using the Full Moon Party guide if an event is part of your trip.

For groups, agree on the return journey before splitting between the town and other areas. For a family stay, ask about the immediate surroundings of the room and how you will reach your chosen beach. Do the same if you are looking for quiet nights: check events near the address for your dates rather than assuming everything outside Haad Rin will be quiet.

Confirm your departure pier with the operating ferry company and allow time to reach it with luggage. The ferry guide is the next planning step, followed by where to stay in Koh Phangan. For the days between arrival and departure, use the four-day itinerary as a starting point and reduce the number of transfers to suit your pace.

beaches.name: Ao Leuk
beaches.tagline: A sandy south-east Koh Tao bay with coral offshore
beaches.summary: Choose Ao Leuk on Koh Tao for a beach visit with a snorkelling focus. Check the visitor route, access arrangements and sea conditions before travelling.
beaches.html:
Ao Leuk is on the south-east coast of Koh Tao. Primary tourism and dive-training pages also use the spelling Aow Leuk. The map pin in this listing identifies the sandy beach, rather than a point offshore, so it is a useful starting place when discussing a drop-off.

SSI describes coral reefs in the bay, while the Koh Tao Tourism Association lists it among the island's popular beaches. It suits a beach plan that leaves time to consider a snorkel, rather than committing you to a deeper dive. Decide what you want from the visit before booking transport: a place on the sand and an in-water session need different preparation.

Make the access part of the plan

  • Ask your accommodation or driver to confirm the visitor entrance, the final drop-off and the return collection point.
  • Carry a way to pay, but ask about any access charge before you travel. No current official admission amount is confirmed here.
  • Check visibility and entry conditions locally. Do not use a general description of the bay as a report on today's water.
  • Take advice on entering without stepping on coral. If you want to practise freediving, use instruction appropriate to your experience rather than improvising from the beach.

Read our snorkelling and freediving guides when deciding which kind of session to plan. Compare Shark Bay for another south-east option, or Tanote Bay before choosing one beach to spend time at. The three-day Koh Tao itinerary keeps beach time alongside the rest of the island.

beaches.name: Bophut Beach
beaches.tagline: Combine Koh Samui’s north-coast sand with Fisherman’s Village
beaches.summary: Visit Bophut Beach on Koh Samui for a shoreline stroll and Fisherman’s Village dining. Treat swimming as a separate decision based on local conditions.
beaches.html:
Bophut Beach is on the north coast of Koh Samui, beside Bophut and Fisherman’s Village. The attraction is the combination of shoreline and village rather than a beach isolated from everything else. Old wooden Chinese shophouses are part of the village’s character, with restaurants and shops giving you reasons to stay after a walk by the water.

Consider a first visit built around the shore and village, then assess the sea separately. Do not book a whole day around a promise of shallow water or calm swimming. Its north-coast position still leaves it on the Gulf, where monsoon weather can change the conditions.

Build the day around the village

  • Try a shoreline walk followed by time in Fisherman’s Village.
  • Check local information for market arrangements. No particular market day or opening time is promised here.
  • Ask before using beachfront seating or facilities; restaurants and hotels set their own arrangements.
  • Follow any beach warnings and choose to stay ashore if conditions are uncertain.

Compare Maenam Beach for another north-coast base, or Chaweng Beach for a different resort atmosphere. The Koh Samui accommodation-area guide helps turn those comparisons into a stay that fits your evenings as well as your beach time.

beaches.name: Bottle Beach (Haad Khuat)
beaches.tagline: A north-coast Koh Phangan beach reached by boat or specialist road transfer
beaches.summary: Plan Bottle Beach on Koh Phangan around the access: a boat from Chaloklum or a specialist four-wheel-drive transfer, with the return agreed in advance.
beaches.html:
Bottle Beach, or Haad Khuat, is on the north coast of Koh Phangan. The sandy bay requires more transport planning than a simple roadside beach stop. Decide how you will leave before you arrive, especially if the visit is part of a day out rather than an overnight stay.

As of November 2026, a beachfront transfer operator explicitly warns that ordinary cars and motorbikes cannot make the final approach: four-wheel drive or a specialist vehicle is needed. Treat that access as an off-road transfer, not a normal scooter descent. Arrange collection with someone who actually serves the beach rather than assuming any taxi can take you to the sand.

Longtail boat or road transfer

  • The sea approach is by boat from Chaloklum. Ask for a longtail transfer to Bottle Beach and agree both legs before setting out.
  • The beachfront operator warns that boats are weather-dependent and are not necessarily waiting at Chaloklum. Confirm service before travelling to the departure point.
  • For the land approach, book the appropriate vehicle in advance. A beach map pin is not evidence that a hired scooter can reach it.
  • Keep enough flexibility to change the visit if your agreed return transport cannot operate.

The Bottle Beach viewpoint is a separate outing to plan, not a substitute drop-off point for the sand. Compare Thong Nai Pan Noi if you prefer to organise an ordinary car transfer. For a longer stay, use our Koh Phangan accommodation guide before committing to this coast.

beaches.name: Chaweng Beach
beaches.tagline: White sand and a social beach day on Koh Samui’s east coast
beaches.summary: Choose Chaweng Beach on Koh Samui for white sand, water sports and an evening out. Its open east-coast setting calls for a fresh sea check each day.
beaches.html:
Chaweng Beach runs along the east coast of Koh Samui. White sand and a developed resort setting make it a practical choice if you want a beach day with somewhere to eat afterwards. The beach and the wider Chaweng area are worth considering together: choose your stretch of sand first, then decide how much evening activity you want around your accommodation.

The Tourism Authority of Thailand describes Chaweng as a centre for water sports by day and nightlife after dark. That gives it a different purpose from a small cove such as Silver Beach. Come here for a social day on the shore, rather than planning on having the beach to yourself. There is no need to hire equipment to enjoy it; a walk followed by a meal is a straightforward way to get your bearings.

Plan the beach around the sea

  • Chaweng faces east into the Gulf. Judge waves at the actual place you intend to enter.
  • The northeast monsoon affects the Gulf. Check the current forecast and beach warnings rather than choosing a swimming day by the calendar.
  • Follow beach warnings and red flags. Keep your plans flexible if the water looks unsettled.
  • Ask before using hotel loungers, toilets or parking. A beachfront location does not establish public access to those services.

Compare Lamai Beach before choosing your base, and use where to stay on Koh Samui to plan the rest of your stay. For a day when swimming is unappealing, browse the island’s attractions.

beaches.tagline: A smaller Koh Samui bay for a beach day near the island’s north-east corner
beaches.summary: Consider Choeng Mon Beach on Koh Samui for a smaller bay and shallow-water setting. Check the day’s conditions instead of treating shelter as a guarantee.
beaches.html:
Choeng Mon Beach lies at the north-east corner of Koh Samui. It offers a smaller-bay setting than the long resort frontage of Chaweng Beach. The local tourism association describes Choeng Mon as shallow and popular with families. Those features make it worth comparing when planning a beach day with children, while keeping supervision and the actual sea conditions central to the decision.

Confirm places to eat, seating and any equipment hire before planning your day around them. Ask what is included if you use a business’s facilities. Bring your own sun cover.

A bay, not a swimming guarantee

  • Shallow water does not establish safe swimming at every tide or in every season.
  • Check local warnings and the Gulf forecast during northeast-monsoon weather.
  • Watch the water at your chosen entry point rather than assuming the whole bay behaves alike.
  • Agree a clear pick-up point and check permitted parking before arriving by vehicle.

Use where to stay on Koh Samui to decide if a smaller bay suits your trip. For a day mixing beach time and sightseeing, consider the island’s Big Buddha Temple and Wat Plai Laem as separate stops, checking their current visitor arrangements before travelling.

beaches.tagline: A southern Koh Tao beach to pair with the John-Suwan viewpoint area
beaches.summary: Plan Freedom Beach on Koh Tao for a southern shore visit near Chalok and John-Suwan Viewpoint. Check current access arrangements and the sea before swimming.

Freedom Beach is at the southern end of Koh Tao, in the Chalok area. Specify the island when asking for directions: this guide covers the Koh Tao beach. The island tourism association includes it among the more accessible beach choices, making it one to consider when dividing a stay between the west-coast village and the southern shore.

Plan a shore visit first, and decide locally whether to add time in the water. Check conditions and ask about equipment and access arrangements before paying for anything. If you also want to visit John-Suwan Viewpoint, confirm the route and admission separately.

Check access before setting out

  • The island tourism association notes that some Koh Tao beaches have access charges. No current Freedom Beach tariff has been confirmed here.
  • Ask what access includes and whether a viewpoint visit requires separate arrangements.
  • Bring suitable footwear if you intend to continue to the viewpoint, plus water and sun protection.
  • The southern setting does not establish calm water throughout the monsoon. Follow warnings and leave swimming optional.

For a beach day without a viewpoint walk, compare Sairee Beach. To see another coast, read about Tanote Bay. The Koh Tao itinerary can help combine these choices without assuming the sea will be suitable at every stop.

beaches.name: Haad Rin Nok (Sunrise Beach)
beaches.tagline: Koh Phangan's Sunrise Beach and Full Moon Party setting
beaches.summary: Choose Haad Rin Nok on Koh Phangan for a beach visit in the same place as the Full Moon Party. Check the event context before choosing your dates.
beaches.html:
Haad Rin Nok, also called Sunrise Beach, is on the south-eastern peninsula of Koh Phangan. It is the Full Moon Party beach, so the first decision is when to visit. Someone looking for the event and someone planning a quiet beach break are choosing the same sand for very different reasons. Use the Haad Rin area guide to put the beach in context before booking accommodation.

The Nok and Nai beaches are separate places. Nok is the Sunrise Beach in this listing, while Nai is on the other side of the peninsula. Give your driver the full name rather than asking only for Haad Rin beach. The map pin here identifies the sandy Nok shoreline, not a ferry landing or the centre of the village.

Plan around the beach you want

  • For the party, read the Full Moon Party page and recheck the announced edition before arranging travel.
  • For a daytime visit, leave time to look at the water before deciding to swim. A party reputation tells you nothing about that day's sea conditions.
  • Agree a return meeting point before splitting up from your group, and keep your onward ferry plans separate from the beach visit.
  • Carry drinking water and sun protection. Lifeguard coverage is not confirmed here.

Compare Haad Yao and Thong Nai Pan Noi when the beach setting matters more than the event. The Koh Phangan accommodation guide helps you decide which coast to use as a base.

beaches.name: Haad Salad
beaches.tagline: A quieter Koh Phangan bay with snorkelling offshore
beaches.summary: Choose Haad Salad on Koh Phangan for a quieter beach setting and an offshore reef. Plan swimming around local conditions and your own ability.
beaches.html:
Haad Salad is on the north-west side of Koh Phangan, north of Haad Yao. The Thai government tourism description singles it out for a quieter atmosphere and snorkelling offshore. It is worth comparing with Haad Yao when you want a bay setting rather than making beach length your main priority.

A reef on a map is not an invitation to swim straight out to it. Decide first how far you are comfortable swimming, what the water is doing and where you can return to shore. Keep your beach plan flexible: sitting by the water and walking the sand are reasonable alternatives to snorkelling when conditions do not suit you.

Before entering the water

  • Ask locally where people enter without crossing coral or shallow rock.
  • Check the water level and wind on arrival. Do not use a calendar month as a promise of safe swimming.
  • Keep the snorkelling guide handy for planning equipment and deciding whether to go with a guide.
  • Carry sun protection and drinking water, and arrange a return meeting place before leaving your transport.

The Srithanu and west-coast guide puts Haad Salad into a wider stay. If you are interested in a shoreline that changes visibly with the water level, compare Mae Haad and the Koh Ma sandbar. For a trip focused on the north-east, read about Thong Nai Pan Noi before deciding where to sleep.

beaches.name: Haad Yao
beaches.tagline: A long white-sand curve on Koh Phangan's west coast
beaches.summary: Use Haad Yao for a west-coast Koh Phangan beach day, with a long white-sand shore and sunset views. Check the water before choosing a swimming spot.
beaches.html:
Haad Yao is on the west coast of Koh Phangan, in the area covered by our Srithanu and west-coast guide. This listing uses the beach mapped as Haad Yao West. Specify that full name when arranging transport.

The municipal description gives a white-sand curve of about a kilometre, with rocky reef areas at either end. The Thai government tourism article also highlights its sunsets. Those details make it a useful choice for a beach walk followed by an evening on the sand. Treat the choice of swimming spot as a separate decision, based on the tide and water conditions when you arrive.

Make a west-coast beach day

  • Use the long shore for a walk before settling on a place to sit, rather than choosing a spot from the road alone.
  • Leave room in your plans for sunset if that is your main reason for choosing this coast.
  • If you want to enter near the rocky ends, ask locally about an appropriate route. Do not make a route across reef.
  • Bring your own sun protection and do not plan your swim around an assumed lifeguard service.

Compare the bay setting at Haad Salad and the sandbar at Mae Haad before adding more stops. Our things to do on Koh Phangan guide helps combine beach time with the rest of the island without changing accommodation every day.

beaches.name: Koh Nang Yuan
beaches.tagline: Three islets and connecting sandbars off Koh Tao, with managed day access
beaches.summary: Plan Koh Nang Yuan from Koh Tao with the operator's day-visitor fee, opening hours and single-use plastic bottle rule checked in November 2026.
beaches.html:
Koh Nang Yuan is the group of three islets connected by sandbars off Koh Tao. The sand connections and the view back across them are the reasons to plan a visit here, rather than treating it as another beach on Koh Tao itself. It requires a boat journey and has managed admission.

For day visitors, as of November 2026, the operator publishes opening hours of 10:00 to 15:00 daily and an entrance fee of THB 250 per person, paid on arrival. Admission outside those hours is restricted to overnight guests. Plan your boat collection around the day-visitor window rather than assuming you can stay for sunset.

Before boarding from Koh Tao

  • As of November 2026, the operator prohibits single-use plastic bottles. Sort out drinking water in a suitable reusable container before leaving.
  • Taxi boats depart from Mae Haad Pier or Sairee Beach on Koh Tao. Agree where you will be collected for the return.
  • Allow time for Koh Nang Yuan viewpoint if that is your priority, rather than leaving it until your boat is due.
  • Ask staff about suitable swimming and snorkelling areas on arrival. Give boats space and keep your beach plans flexible.

A self-arranged boat lets you discuss the return directly; an organised excursion needs its own inclusions checked before purchase. Do not assume the landing fee is included in a boat quote. Compare a shore-based visit to Ao Leuk if you would prefer to stay on Koh Tao, and use the Koh Tao itinerary to leave room for the journey.

beaches.name: Lamai Beach
beaches.tagline: A curved Koh Samui bay with a town behind it and rocks at its southern end
beaches.summary: Plan Lamai Beach on Koh Samui for a sandy bay with places to eat and the Hin Ta and Hin Yai rocks. Check the sea before planning a swim.
beaches.html:
Lamai Beach is on the east coast of Koh Samui, south of Chaweng. Its curved shoreline, coconut palms and places to eat make it an option for travellers who want to spend time in a beach town as well as on the sand. Read the Lamai area guide before choosing accommodation: the destination is more than a single swimming spot.

The Tourism Authority of Thailand describes deeper water at Lamai. Keep that general description separate from conditions at your chosen entry point. A broad sandy bay does not mean that every section has the same depth or exposure. Look at the water where you are, ask about the day’s conditions and follow any warnings rather than copying the behaviour of other swimmers.

A flexible day at Lamai

  • Keep an east-coast beach plan flexible during northeast-monsoon weather.
  • Choose a shore walk or a meal if the waves make swimming unappealing.
  • Bring your own sun protection. Confirm access before using any beachfront business’s facilities.
  • Visit the Hin Ta and Hin Yai rocks at the southern end as a separate sightseeing stop.

For a smaller bay, compare Silver Beach. If you are deciding between beach towns, put Lamai beside Chaweng Beach and read where to stay on Koh Samui. Neither choice should depend on a promise of safe swimming throughout your trip.

beaches.name: Lipa Noi Beach
beaches.tagline: A west-facing Koh Samui shore for sunset and a tide-aware beach day
beaches.summary: Plan Lipa Noi Beach on Koh Samui for a west-coast shore visit and sunset. Shallow water and changing tides can limit swimming depth along the beach.
beaches.html:
Lipa Noi Beach is on the west coast of Koh Samui. The west-facing shoreline makes it a place to consider for the end of a beach day, with the sunset ahead of you rather than behind the island. It provides a different coastal orientation from Chaweng and Lamai, both on the east.

A beachfront operator’s account describes soft sand and a shallow entry, while stressing that depth varies with the tide and the exact stretch of shore. It also describes deeper water beside its own frontage. That is useful evidence of variation, not a reason to go searching for a swimming channel. If swimming matters to your visit, ask about the water at the specific place you intend to enter and check the tide before committing to the afternoon.

Make room for the tide

  • At low tide, some shallow sections may not have enough depth for comfortable swimming. Plan for time on the sand as well.
  • Keep children under close supervision even at a shallow edge.
  • A west-coast position does not rule out rough weather. Check conditions during northeast-monsoon periods as well as at other times.
  • Bring water and sun protection, and confirm your chosen access and return transport.

For a day ashore, consider Nathon town as another west-coast stop. For more days, the Koh Samui five-day itinerary gives you a framework to adapt around weather and transport.

beaches.name: Mae Haad Beach (Koh Ma sandbar)
beaches.tagline: Koh Phangan's north-west beach beside the Koh Ma sandbar
beaches.summary: Visit Mae Haad on Koh Phangan for white sand and the tidal sandbar towards Koh Ma. Check the water level before deciding whether to cross.
beaches.html:
Mae Haad Beach is on the north-west coast of Koh Phangan, beside the small island of Koh Ma. This listing is not Mae Haad on Koh Tao. Use the island name when organising a trip, particularly if your holiday includes both islands.

The municipal description gives Mae Haad a length of about 800 metres. The government tourism article describes fine white sand and a sandbar towards Koh Ma that becomes exposed as the water recedes. The changing connection is the reason to check the actual water level rather than arrive expecting a permanent dry path.

Plan for a changing shoreline

  • Look at the sandbar and water conditions before deciding to cross. If the route is covered or conditions look uncertain, enjoy the view from the beach.
  • Do not use a seasonal description as a tide prediction for your visit.
  • Keep an eye on your return route if you walk towards Koh Ma, and turn back before access becomes doubtful.
  • For snorkelling, ask about suitable entry and current conditions rather than crossing reef to reach deeper water.

Mae Haad makes a different sort of outing from Haad Salad or Haad Yao: watching the shoreline change can be enough of a reason to visit without entering the sea. Consult the Koh Phangan activities guide to choose a sensible combination, and leave enough time for your agreed transport back.

What to check on arrival

  • Maenam’s north-facing position describes its exposure, not a guarantee of calm water.
  • Check the sea and local warnings before swimming, especially when northeast-monsoon weather affects the Gulf.

The Sairee and Mae Haad guide helps distinguish the beach area from the island’s arrival area. The tourism association recommends the beachside walking street for the walk from Mae Haad rather than the main road. If you choose to walk, carry water and take your time. No fixed journey time is needed to make that decision, and a clear meeting point is still useful if you arrange transport instead.

A social base with a flexible beach plan

  • Consider Sairee for shore time, food and evening activity, rather than a secluded-cove experience.
  • Its west-coast position does not establish safe swimming at every tide. Check the sea before entering.

  • Ask venues about equipment, seating and facilities rather than assuming they are public.

beaches.tagline: A south-east Koh Tao bay for a beach visit and shore snorkelling
beaches.summary: Plan Shark Bay on Koh Tao as a south-east beach and snorkelling stop. Confirm visitor access, then choose a water entry that suits the conditions.
beaches.html:
Shark Bay, also called Ao Thian Ok, is on the south-east corner of Koh Tao. Local pages also spell the bay Thian Og. Use Shark Bay together with the island name when arranging transport, rather than relying on the translated name alone.

The Koh Tao Tourism Association includes it among the island's shore-snorkelling beaches. That makes it a place to investigate if you want time in the water without making the whole day a boat excursion. The name is not a wildlife guarantee. This guide gives no animal timetable or promised sighting, so plan a visit you would still enjoy without seeing a shark.

Access and time in the water

  • A beachfront operator describes both taxi and taxi-boat access from Mae Haad. Ask the driver or skipper to confirm where you will arrive.
  • Confirm the visitor route and any charge before setting out. A transfer to accommodation does not by itself establish unrestricted day-visitor access through that property.
  • Use the snorkelling guide to think through equipment, flotation and whether you would prefer a guided session.
  • Check wind, visibility and a suitable way back out before entering, and stay within your swimming ability.

Compare Ao Leuk when choosing a south-east beach visit. For a separate land outing, read about John-Suwan viewpoint rather than assuming it shares the same entrance. Our Koh Tao guide helps fit the visit around the rest of your stay.

beaches.name: Silver Beach (Haad Thong Ta-khian)
beaches.tagline: Koh Samui’s granite-framed cove, also called Crystal Bay
beaches.summary: Find Silver Beach on Koh Samui between Chaweng and Lamai: white sand, granite boulders and a compact cove for a shore visit when sea conditions allow.
beaches.html:
Silver Beach is a small cove on the east coast of Koh Samui, between Chaweng and Lamai. Its Thai name is Haad Thong Ta-khian, and Crystal Bay is another name for the same place. Use those names when checking directions so that a different label on a map does not send you looking for a second beach.

The local tourism association describes a beach about 250 metres long, with granite boulders and shallow water. A beachfront operator describes white sand and a path down from the coastal road. The appeal is the shape of the cove: you can see the rocky boundaries rather than looking along a long resort shoreline. It is worth considering as a beach stop from Lamai or Chaweng, without needing to move your base.

Swimming and a shore visit

  • Tourism descriptions mention swimming and shore snorkelling. Make either activity conditional on what the sea is doing when you arrive.
  • The bay faces the Gulf from the east coast. Its rocks do not justify a promise of calm water throughout the northeast monsoon.
  • Use the sandy shore for entry rather than treating the boulders as a diving platform.
  • Ask about access and facility use before using a private venue’s seating or parking.

Take a look at the snorkelling guide if you are bringing a mask. For a larger beach-town day, compare Lamai Beach. Keep the plan flexible enough to enjoy the cove from the sand if swimming conditions are poor.

beaches.tagline: An east-coast Koh Tao bay for a shore visit away from Sairee
beaches.summary: Visit Tanote Bay on Koh Tao for an east-coast beach setting away from Sairee. Plan for the bay’s exposure and make swimming conditional on the day’s sea.
beaches.html:
Tanote Bay is on the east coast of Koh Tao. The island tourism association places it among the eastern bays with coastal accommodation, giving it a different setting from the west-coast village of Sairee. Consider a shore visit even if swimming is left out of the day’s plan.

The tourism association includes Tanote among Koh Tao’s more accessible beach choices, with food and drink options in that group of beaches. Confirm the services you need at your chosen access rather than treating the whole bay as a managed public beach. If you plan to stay for a meal, check the venue before settling on the sand. Arrange the return journey at the same time as the outward one.

Let the east-coast exposure guide you

  • Look at the waves across the bay before choosing an entry point. A cove shape alone does not prove shelter.
  • During northeast-monsoon weather, follow the Gulf forecast and beach warnings rather than assuming the east side will be calm.
  • No supervised jumping arrangement or safe water depth has been verified. Leave jumping out of your plan.
  • Bring water and sun cover. Public showers, toilets and lifeguards have not been verified.

Read the snorkelling guide before planning any time in the water, and compare Sairee or Freedom Beach for another outing. Keep a choice of coasts in your Koh Tao itinerary rather than fixing every beach visit before checking the weather.

beaches.tagline: The northern Thong Nai Pan bay on Koh Phangan, with road transfers available
beaches.summary: Choose Thong Nai Pan Noi on Koh Phangan for a sandy north-east bay with car transfers available. Specify Noi when arranging arrival at the twin bays.
beaches.html:
Thong Nai Pan Noi is the northern of the two Thong Nai Pan bays on the north-east coast of Koh Phangan. The mapped beach lies north of Thong Nai Pan Yai. Specify Noi when arranging transport, since a booking or drop-off described simply as Thong Nai Pan leaves the final bay unclear.

The beachfront operator's arrival page currently offers a car transfer from the island pier. This is a beach you can arrange to reach by road, without relying on a longtail boat. A complete current surface assessment for the approach road was not confirmed. Ask your driver about the day's route and any damage before setting off, rather than treating old dirt-track descriptions as a current road report.

Arrange the final part of the journey

  • Send your arrival pier and the full beach name when booking a road transfer.
  • Confirm the actual collection point and return arrangement, particularly for a day visit.
  • If considering a longtail, ask a local boat operator about availability and conditions first. No scheduled longtail service is confirmed here.
  • Plan to assess the sea when you arrive. A sheltered-looking bay does not establish safe conditions on a particular day.

The Thong Nai Pan area guide helps you compare the twin bays. A beachfront operator describes powdery sand at Noi, making a simple beach stay a reasonable focus without adding a new outing every day. Compare access at Bottle Beach before treating it as an easy extension. Start with the four-day itinerary once your base is settled.
